Origin: T01/05 handoff (`LLM-20261017-009-T01-WORKER-05`) and T02/07 review-01 (`LLM-20261017-010-T02-REVIEW-01`).  
Status: coordinator decision from explicit preconditions in `requirements/AI_Challenge_14.md`; no transition, role, error text, or cycle limit is changed. The initial version's document-merge ambiguity was found in `LLM-20261017-010-T00-REVIEW-AD01` and resolved below.

## Claim facts

`ClaimFacts` contains business data from authenticated claim actors. Before evaluation, the service validates the submitted patch shape, authorizes every changed field against the authenticated actor and current claim, then merges it with persisted facts and writes the merged facts atomically with a successful claim mutation. Other top-level facts use shallow replacement (a supplied value replaces that top-level value); the `documents` map uses the field-level merge rule below. Missing, malformed, wrongly typed, or unauthorized fields fail closed without mutation.

| Fact key | Shape and guard use | Who may assert or change it |
|---|---|---|
| `documents` | Non-empty object keyed by stable document ID (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,119}`), with boolean `required`, `present`, and `valid` fields per entry. At least one entry must be required; every required document must be present and valid. | `document_clerk` creates roster entries and sets `required`, `valid`, and `present`. The claim-owning member can update only `present` on an existing document ID. Entries are never deleted. |
| `assessorId` | Nonblank string. | `team_lead`. |
| `assessmentReport` | Object with boolean `complete`; only literal `true` passes. | `assessor`. |
| `requestedAmount` | Exact decimal JSON number, nonnegative, no more than `Claim.policyLimit`. Currency is the claim's immutable currency. | Set at claim creation; immutable afterward. |

The transition `reason` is the rejection reason for `rejection_reason_present` and the missing-information description for `information_description_present`; it is also the user-supplied audit note. Both guards require nonblank text. `TransitionCommand.suppliedFacts` cannot set server-owned evidence fields.

Document updates merge by document ID and then by field: an authorized partial update to `present` preserves the existing `required` and `valid` values. Omitted document IDs and omitted fields preserve their stored values. Null document entries or null fields are rejected; there is no delete operation for a roster entry. Members cannot add, remove, rename, or modify document roster entries, and cannot send `required` or `valid`; such attempts are rejected. Clerks may add entries while the claim is `SUBMITTED` or `PENDING_INFO`, including newly requested documents; existing entries are never removed or renamed. The `required` flag on an existing entry can be changed only while the claim is `SUBMITTED`; it is immutable afterward. A clerk may change `present` or `valid` while the claim is `SUBMITTED` or `PENDING_INFO`. No list-index identity or recursive merge is used.

## Server-owned workflow evidence

The service constructs an immutable `WorkflowEvidence` from database state; it is never deserialized from request facts. Timestamps are truncated to PostgreSQL microsecond precision when written and compared at that precision.

| Evidence | Source and update rule |
|---|---|
| `informationRequests`, `lastInformationRequestedAt` | Claim row. Increment and stamp atomically when the configured cycle-policy transition succeeds. The configured maximum remains three; attempt four returns the exact configured message. |
| `lastInformationReceivedAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it from injected `Clock` when authenticated member-owned new information is persisted while the claim is `PENDING_INFO`; request timestamps are ignored. |
| `assessmentStartedAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it when `record_assessment_start` succeeds. |
| `rejectedAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it in the successful `UNDER_ASSESSMENT -> REJECTED` transaction. |
| `memberAcknowledgedRejectionAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it only for the authenticated owner member's explicit acknowledgement while the claim is `REJECTED`; a request boolean is an action signal, never a timestamp. |
| payment-request/confirmation evidence | `payment_requests` row. Only the service/mock payment adapter writes a request, confirmation timestamp, and reference. Client facts cannot assert a request or confirmation. |

The engine receives `WorkflowEvaluationContext(Claim claim, Actor actor, TransitionCommand command, WorkflowEvidence evidence, Instant now, Duration appealPeriod)`. It is pure: it reads the persisted claim, the already-authorized business-fact merge, and server-built evidence; it performs no I/O or writes.

## Guard semantics

- `all_required_documents_present`: validate the `documents` shape and the required-document rule above.
- `assessor_assigned`: `assessorId` is a nonblank string.
- `assessment_report_complete`: `assessmentReport.complete` is exactly `true`.
- `amount_within_policy_limit`: `requestedAmount` is an exact decimal, nonnegative and at most the claim policy limit.
- `rejection_reason_present` and `information_description_present`: transition reason is nonblank.
- `new_information_received`: server-stamped `lastInformationReceivedAt` is strictly after `lastInformationRequestedAt`.
- `payment_request_exists`: a persisted payment request exists for the claim.
- `payment_confirmed`: the persisted payment request has a nonblank reference and server-stamped confirmation time.
- `appeal_period_expired_or_member_acknowledged`: either `now >= rejectedAt + appealPeriod`, or an owner-member acknowledgement timestamp is at/after `rejectedAt`.

The appeal duration is `claims.workflow.appeal-period`, environment override `CLAIMS_APPEAL_PERIOD`, default `P30D`. The challenge specifies expiry behavior but no duration; 30 days is the documented configurable local default, not a claimed external policy.

The engine resolves configured guard/effect IDs through strategy registries; it does not branch on state names. A configured cycle policy selects the transition ID, counter and exact error message. Duplicate state/transition IDs, duplicate `(from,to)` pairs, dangling states, unknown roles/strategies and malformed configuration fail startup. A state/edge extension using existing roles, guards and effects remains configuration-only.

## Persistence/API seams

- Typed `ClaimAggregate` combines the public `Claim` value with `ClaimWorkflowData`; API DTOs do not expose server metadata.
- `ClaimWorkflowData` stores the cycle counter and trusted timestamps in the claim row. Payment evidence stays in `payment_requests`.
- `ClaimRepository` compare-and-set writes the claim and workflow data under one transaction/version check. Domain audit, idempotency receipt, payment, system audit and outbox writes share the same transaction.
- Runtime grants are explicit by table. `claims_runtime` cannot UPDATE or DELETE either audit table and cannot alter immutable identifiers/payload columns in payment/outbox rows. No broad `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants are used.
- PostgreSQL Testcontainers must create distinct migration/runtime roles and verify actual grants, rollback, concurrency and exact JSON numeric behavior. Static source inspection is not database evidence.

4. Workers read source and draft candidate.patch plus handoff.json in their own

# T02 / attempt 11 independent review

**Verdict: REWORK.** The adapter draft is substantially scoped to the approved paths and maps the six ports, but the claim CAS violates immutable aggregate fields and the sole IT does not establish several advertised persistence/security properties. No build, test, Docker, database, or Git mutation was run; compilation and runtime behavior remain unverified. `PARTIAL` is an accurate handoff/audit status, and this review does not accept T02 or the application.

## Findings

1. **[High] CAS rewrites immutable ownership and policy values.** In `candidate.patch:444-450`, `compareAndSet` sets `member_id`, `policy_limit`, and `currency` from the supplied aggregate while only comparing `id` and `version`. A stale or incorrectly composed aggregate can therefore transfer ownership or change the coverage limit/currency through an ordinary workflow update. Restrict this update to mutable workflow fields (and state/facts as contractually mutable), leaving immutable columns untouched; add an assertion that these fields cannot change through CAS. Schema ownership/values originate in changeset 001 (`src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-initial-schema.sql:4-10`).

2. **[High] IT elevates the Liquibase migration login to SUPERUSER.** `candidate.patch:554-565` provisions `claims_migration` as `SUPERUSER`, then runs Liquibase with it. This bypasses the schema-owner boundary that changeset 002 explicitly assumes (`src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/002-persistence.sql:87-98`) and cannot verify least-privilege migration/runtime grants. Provision a non-superuser schema owner with only the required ownership/DDL rights, then prove the runtime connection remains limited to its grants.

3. **[Medium] Audit IT does not test append-only protection.** The test at `candidate.patch:590-596` only inserts two rows and checks ordering; it never attempts UPDATE/DELETE under the runtime role or verifies the trigger/grants reject them. Add database assertions for both mutations and retain the existing deterministic ordering assertion. Changeset 002 installs the trigger and grants at lines 77-98.

4. **[Medium] Claimed idempotency/outbox IT coverage is only a happy-path smoke check.** `candidate.patch:598-606` reads back one receipt and claims/delivers one outbox row, but does not test duplicate-key conflict/replay, changed-fingerprint conflict, concurrent `SKIP LOCKED` ownership, retry/error behavior, or payment persistence/confirmation. The packet specifically requires dedicated `AuditImmutabilityIT`, `IdempotencyIT`, and `PaymentOutboxIT`; they are absent, as the handoff also discloses. Add those focused ITs before treating the adapters as persistence-verified.

5. **[Low] Outbox lease is fixed in SQL.** `candidate.patch:473-478` hard-codes a 30-second lease, while failure retry is passed by the caller and configuration currently exposes dispatch/retry delays (`src/main/resources/application.yml`, `claims.outbox`). Make lease duration an explicit configured/bound value or document and contractually fix it; test a lease expiry/reclaim boundary. The handoff correctly flags this as requiring coordinator review.

## Inspected areas

- All declared patch paths are within the task's approved mapper, persistence, SQL-resource, and persistence-test directories; no attempt to edit shared ports/migrations is present.
- Port method shapes align with adapter implementations by inspection. `@Mapper` annotations plus the configured MyBatis starter and mapper resource glob appear consistent; the host application wiring/compilation has not been exercised.
- JSON uses the configured `ObjectMapper`, JSONB text casts, and `use-big-decimal-for-floats`; policy values use `BigDecimal`. This is a plausible exact-decimal path, but the IT cannot prove it until run.
- Claim pagination and count queries use the same member predicate and stable `created_at DESC, id` ordering. Audit reads use sequence/id ordering. The outbox CTE uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and atomically advances availability/attempts.
- Handoff accurately records missing dedicated IT sources, unrun runtime verification, fixed lease, and host payload capture as `NOT_CAPTURED` / `PARTIAL`.

**Verdict: REWORK.** Least-privilege role provisioning is materially improved and the requested cases are represented, but most integration tests issue SQL that reproduces the production mapper statements instead of invoking the current MyBatis mapper/adapters. The outbox claim CTE in `PaymentOutboxIT.java:36-39` hard-codes a 30-second lease and SQL shape, rather than calling `MyBatisOutboxRepository.claimDue` / `EffectsMapper.claimDue` (the current mapper binds `leaseMillis` at `src/main/resources/sql/service/claim/EffectsMapper.xml`, `claimDue`). 2. **[Medium] Idempotency assertions cover storage constraints only.** `IdempotencyIT.java:14-30` verifies one receipt, JSONB equality, and that a duplicate insert throws `SQLException`; it does not invoke `MyBatisIdempotencyRepository.find/insert` or test the adapter's domain-object mapping. 3. **[Medium] CAS regression is partly textual and the database mutation is not CAS.** `ClaimPersistenceIT.java:33-40` inspects the packaged XML for the absence of immutable column names in the `<update>`, while `:44-65` runs a handwritten state/version update. ## Claim facts

`ClaimFacts` contains business data from authenticated claim actors. Before evaluation, the service validates the submitted patch shape, authorizes every changed field against the authenticated actor and current claim, then merges it with persisted facts and writes the merged facts atomically with a successful claim mutation. Other top-level facts use shallow replacement (a supplied value replaces that top-level value); the `documents` map uses the field-level merge rule below. Missing, malformed, wrongly typed, or unauthorized fields fail closed without mutation.

| Fact key | Shape and guard use | Who may assert or change it |
|---|---|---|
| `documents` | Non-empty object keyed by stable document ID (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,119}`), with boolean `required`, `present`, and `valid` fields per entry. At least one entry must be required; every required document must be present and valid. | `document_clerk` creates roster entries and sets `required`, `valid`, and `present`. The claim-owning member can update only `present` on an existing document ID. Entries are never deleted. |
| `assessorId` | Nonblank string. | `team_lead`. |
| `assessmentReport` | Object with boolean `complete`; only literal `true` passes. | `assessor`. |
| `requestedAmount` | Exact decimal JSON number, nonnegative, no more than `Claim.policyLimit`. Currency is the claim's immutable currency. | Set at claim creation; immutable afterward. |

The transition `reason` is the rejection reason for `rejection_reason_present` and the missing-information description for `information_description_present`; it is also the user-supplied audit note. Both guards require nonblank text. `TransitionCommand.suppliedFacts` cannot set server-owned evidence fields.

Document updates merge by document ID and then by field: an authorized partial update to `present` preserves the existing `required` and `valid` values. Omitted document IDs and omitted fields preserve their stored values. Null document entries or null fields are rejected; there is no delete operation for a roster entry. Members cannot add, remove, rename, or modify document roster entries, and cannot send `required` or `valid`; such attempts are rejected. Clerks may add entries while the claim is `SUBMITTED` or `PENDING_INFO`, including newly requested documents; existing entries are never removed or renamed. The `required` flag on an existing entry can be changed only while the claim is `SUBMITTED`; it is immutable afterward. A clerk may change `present` or `valid` while the claim is `SUBMITTED` or `PENDING_INFO`. No list-index identity or recursive merge is used.

## Server-owned workflow evidence

The service constructs an immutable `WorkflowEvidence` from database state; it is never deserialized from request facts. Timestamps are truncated to PostgreSQL microsecond precision when written and compared at that precision.

| Evidence | Source and update rule |
|---|---|
| `informationRequests`, `lastInformationRequestedAt` | Claim row. Increment and stamp atomically when the configured cycle-policy transition succeeds. The configured maximum remains three; attempt four returns the exact configured message. |
| `lastInformationReceivedAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it from injected `Clock` when authenticated member-owned new information is persisted while the claim is `PENDING_INFO`; request timestamps are ignored. |
| `assessmentStartedAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it when `record_assessment_start` succeeds. |
| `rejectedAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it in the successful `UNDER_ASSESSMENT -> REJECTED` transaction. |
| `memberAcknowledgedRejectionAt` | Claim row. Service stamps it only for the authenticated owner member's explicit acknowledgement while the claim is `REJECTED`; a request boolean is an action signal, never a timestamp. |
| payment-request/confirmation evidence | `payment_requests` row. Only the service/mock payment adapter writes a request, confirmation timestamp, and reference. Client facts cannot assert a request or confirmation. |

The engine receives `WorkflowEvaluationContext(Claim claim, Actor actor, TransitionCommand command, WorkflowEvidence evidence, Instant now, Duration appealPeriod)`. It is pure: it reads the persisted claim, the already-authorized business-fact merge, and server-built evidence; it performs no I/O or writes.

## Guard semantics

- `all_required_documents_present`: validate the `documents` shape and the required-document rule above.
- `assessor_assigned`: `assessorId` is a nonblank string.
- `assessment_report_complete`: `assessmentReport.complete` is exactly `true`.
- `amount_within_policy_limit`: `requestedAmount` is an exact decimal, nonnegative and at most the claim policy limit.
- `rejection_reason_present` and `information_description_present`: transition reason is nonblank.
- `new_information_received`: server-stamped `lastInformationReceivedAt` is strictly after `lastInformationRequestedAt`.
- `payment_request_exists`: a persisted payment request exists for the claim.
- `payment_confirmed`: the persisted payment request has a nonblank reference and server-stamped confirmation time.
- `appeal_period_expired_or_member_acknowledged`: either `now >= rejectedAt + appealPeriod`, or an owner-member acknowledgement timestamp is at/after `rejectedAt`.

The appeal duration is `claims.workflow.appeal-period`, environment override `CLAIMS_APPEAL_PERIOD`, default `P30D`. The challenge specifies expiry behavior but no duration; 30 days is the documented configurable local default, not a claimed external policy.

The engine resolves configured guard/effect IDs through strategy registries; it does not branch on state names. A configured cycle policy selects the transition ID, counter and exact error message. Duplicate state/transition IDs, duplicate `(from,to)` pairs, dangling states, unknown roles/strategies and malformed configuration fail startup. A state/edge extension using existing roles, guards and effects remains configuration-only.

## Persistence/API seams

- Typed `ClaimAggregate` combines the public `Claim` value with `ClaimWorkflowData`; API DTOs do not expose server metadata.
- `ClaimWorkflowData` stores the cycle counter and trusted timestamps in the claim row. Payment evidence stays in `payment_requests`.
- `ClaimRepository` compare-and-set writes the claim and workflow data under one transaction/version check. Domain audit, idempotency receipt, payment, system audit and outbox writes share the same transaction.
- Runtime grants are explicit by table. `claims_runtime` cannot UPDATE or DELETE either audit table and cannot alter immutable identifiers/payload columns in payment/outbox rows. No broad `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants are used.
- PostgreSQL Testcontainers must create distinct migration/runtime roles and verify actual grants, rollback, concurrency and exact JSON numeric behavior. Static source inspection is not database evidence.

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Claims Workflow API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Secured single-service claims workflow API. Correlation IDs use X-Correlation-ID and are separate from tracing identifiers.
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:8080/api/v1
security:
  - basicAuth: []
paths:
  /claims:
    get:
      summary: List visible claims
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Page'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Size'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Paged claims visible to the authenticated actor
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ClaimPage' }
        '401': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
    post:
      summary: Create a claim
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateClaimRequest' }
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Claim created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Claim' }
        '409': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    get:
      summary: Get a claim
      responses:
        '200':

API DTOs remain in `claim/api/dto`; transport maps `TransitionResult` to `TransitionResultView { claim, audit, replayed }`. Create and response policy limits are nonnegative PostgreSQL `NUMERIC(18,2)` values: at most 16 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. Currency is exactly three uppercase ASCII letters. Facts are bounded JSON objects with recursively immutable domain representation.

Collection reads use zero-based page (default 0) and size (default 20, max 100), return `{items,total,page,size,totalPages}`, share count/page predicates, and have deterministic ordering. Member filtering is in SQL. The `X-Correlation-ID` header accepts at most 128 safe ASCII characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; invalid or absent values become a generated UUID. Return the effective value in the response and structured logs/MDC. Correlation IDs are distinct from tracing IDs. Mutation routes require an `Idempotency-Key`; identical actor/scope/key/fingerprint requests replay the stored result, while key reuse with a different fingerprint is a stable conflict.

## Workflow boundary

The resource `config/workflow.yml` is frozen under T00. It has eight initial states, nine original edges, ten guard IDs, ten effect IDs, and a maximum of three information requests. Preserve all configured role, guard, effect, and error text. New transitions/states must be expressible from existing configured primitives without adding state-specific engine branches. Guards consume trusted, persisted claim facts and server-owned receipt/payment/appeal metadata. Request-supplied values cannot spoof a server-stamped receipt or payment confirmation.

The engine is pure with respect to persistence and HTTP. It determines available choices and validates a requested configured transition. It returns decisions/effect identifiers; the transactional service persists domain changes and durable local outbox/payment/audit records. External mock effects run only after commit.

AD-01 resolves the fact/evidence and persistence seams without changing states,
edges, roles, guard/effect IDs, configured error messages, or the three-cycle
limit. Its exact semantics and domain types are in
[`FACTS-AND-PERSISTENCE.md`](./FACTS-AND-PERSISTENCE.md). The decision originated
from the T01/05 blocked handoff and T02/07 independent review, recorded in the
append-only interaction log.

## Persistence and atomicity

Liquibase 001 creates the base `claims` table. T02 adds schema in a new changeset and updates the master changelog through coordinator integration. Required stores are `claim_audit`, `system_operation_audit`, idempotency/command receipts, payment requests, and local outbox. Successful claim state, domain audit, successful system-operation audit, idempotency result, payment request and outbox changes commit atomically. Claim writes use row locking or version compare-and-set. Audit records are append-only, have no cascading claim-delete relationship, and runtime permissions/triggers deny UPDATE/DELETE. Runtime credentials cannot perform DDL or change migration ownership.

The system-operation audit contains action, resource/resource ID, authenticated actor, correlation ID, outcome, safe error type and timestamp. It never serializes method arguments by default. A successful audited write cannot commit if its audit insert fails. A separately committed failure audit must preserve the original business exception. Idempotency scope includes actor plus operation/resource; fingerprints use a canonical request form and never include credentials.

## Evidence and completion

Worker attempts write only candidate patches and handoffs under their exclusive attempt directories. The coordinator alone applies source patches, runs builds/DB/Docker/Git operations and edits shared docs/manifest/memory. Independent reviewers are read-only. Host-managed model payload fields unavailable from the runtime are `NOT_CAPTURED`; their audit is `PARTIAL`. No application verification, migration success, startup readiness, capacity, or production readiness is claimed without actual evidence.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# The official image runs init scripts only on first database creation.
# psql variable quoting safely handles generated passwords without logging them.
psql --username "$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname "$POSTGRES_DB" \
  --set=migration_user="$CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_USER" \
  --set=migration_password="[REDACTED_SECRET]" \
  --set=runtime_user="$CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_USER" \
  --set=runtime_password="[REDACTED_SECRET]" <<'SQL'
SELECT format('CREATE ROLE %I LOGIN PASSWORD %L NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT', :'migration_user', :'migration_password')
\gexec
SELECT format('CREATE ROLE %I LOGIN PASSWORD %L NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT', :'runtime_user', :'runtime_password')
\gexec
ALTER DATABASE claims OWNER TO :"migration_user";
ALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO :"migration_user";
REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE claims TO :"migration_user", :"runtime_user";
GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO :"migration_user";
SQL

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

env_file=.env
example=.env.example
if [[ ! -f "$env_file" ]]; then
  cp "$example" "$env_file"
  chmod 600 "$env_file"
fi

replace_dummy() {
  local key=$1 value
  value=$(awk -F= -v key="$key" '$1 == key { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; found=1; exit } END { if (!found) exit 1 }' "$env_file") || {
    echo "Missing $key in .env" >&2
    return 1
  }
  if [[ "$value" == CHANGE_ME_* || -z "$value" ]]; then
    value=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
    sed -i "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$env_file"
  fi
}

replace_dummy CLAIMS_BOOTSTRAP_DB_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD
chmod 600 "$env_file"

compose=(docker compose --env-file "$env_file" -f docker/compose.yml)
"${compose[@]}" config --quiet
"${compose[@]}" up -d --build --wait --wait-timeout 180
echo "Claims services are healthy. Run bash scripts/smoke.sh to verify the API."
CLAIMS_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://database:5432/claims
CLAIMS_BOOTSTRAP_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET]

CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET]

SERVER_PORT=8080
CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET]
CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET]
3:The intended local runtime uses Docker Compose with PostgreSQL 16, a bootstrap credential used only by database initialization, a non-superuser migration login that owns the application schema, and a restricted runtime login. The runtime login receives table-specific grants; audit tables have append-only triggers, and payment/outbox updates are column-scoped. This is implemented as migration/configuration source but has not yet been exercised against PostgreSQL. The bootstrap password is generated by `scripts/setup.sh`; production secrets must not be committed or placed in the sample environment.

As written, applying it after attempt 13 encounters existing paths and fails. I did not run `git apply --check` because this review was required to remain read-only and avoid Git operations.

# Coordinator and worker workflow

Coordinator: gpt-6.1-sol / medium. Every implementation and review subagent:
gpt-6-luna / medium. Use at most three concurrent subagents outside the coordinator,
subject to host limits. Pass explicit model/effort and fresh context when spawning.
Instructions alone do not change the active primary model or host permissions.

## Requirement loop

1. Read rules/REQUIREMENT.md, applicable rules, current docs/history and authoritative
   memory progress. For **each** new human message, append the verbatim prompt to
   `docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` and a dated requirement-change entry to
   `rules/REQUIREMENT.md` **before** implementation, even for follow-up requests.
   Establish append-only interaction evidence recording before dispatch. Enforce
   full pre-dispatch request capture for directly managed/model API calls; for
   host-managed calls preserve accessible task packets and execution evidence
   and document any unavailable raw payloads as NOT_CAPTURED.
2. Update acceptance criteria, to-do/DAG, inputs/outputs, exclusive patch paths,
   required checks and estimate. Freeze/compile shared interfaces before consumers.
3. For directly controlled LLM API invocations (including workers, reviewers and
   retries), persist the actual outbound request before dispatch and the inbound
   response/error/partial output afterward; fail closed if pre-dispatch request
   logging is unavailable. For host-managed coordinator/worker/reviewer calls,
   persist every exposed task packet, input/output, model/attempt metadata and
   review artifact. If the host hides raw model payloads, record the affected
   interaction ID, reason and `NOT_CAPTURED` fields, set audit status `PARTIAL`,
   and continue authorized dispatch (no fabrication or COMPLETE audit claim).
   Link interactions -> requirements -> tasks/attempts. Protect secrets, dispatch
   only when dependencies are accepted, and pass source/contract hashes, role
   and exclusive task/attempt artifact directory.
4. Workers read source and draft candidate.patch plus handoff.json in their own
   artifact directory. They do not modify source, plans, memory or build output,
   run builds/Docker/DB/Git mutations, or spawn other agents.
5. Coordinator checks patch target ownership, base/contract hashes and full content,
   dry-runs the patch and applies it serially. Rebase stale patches before apply.
6. Coordinator runs focused checks, captures command/exit code/source hash/report,
   prints test progress and fixes core causes through the owning worker.
7. A fresh independent reviewer inspects actual source/assertions/results and
   reports criteria coverage and actionable findings with file:line. Resolve
   correctness/security/requirement findings and rereview affected changes.
8. Coordinator verifies interaction evidence and independent-review trace links,
   recording missing host-managed payloads as `NOT_CAPTURED` and audit `PARTIAL`.
   `PARTIAL` alone does not prohibit implementation acceptance, provided mandatory
   tests pass, review is independent, source/evidence match, and no explicit full-
   capture acceptance condition remains unmet. Never report full traceability when
   any required payload is missing. Coordinator accepts only when
   every required command has final PASS/exit0 and other gates are satisfied. Update manifest,
   checklist, memory and synchronized history after acceptance.
9. Run final integrated gates/review, update current architecture/runbook/history,
   and prepare source/config/scenarios/audit/diff/raw-conversation submission.

## One source writer

Workers write only rules/workflow/artifacts/TASK/ATTEMPT/. allowed_paths in the manifest
constrain the intended patch targets, not direct filesystem edits. Coordinator
owns source/shared files and serializes builds, database and Docker operations.
Independent task paths cannot overlap or contain one another. Shared ports,
pom/application YAML/changelog/manifest/memory changes go through the coordinator.

and integration tests address semantic conflicts. Agent instructions are a
protocol, not an independently enforced filesystem sandbox.

planned → running → submitted → in_review → accepted. Failures require rework;
unavailable prerequisites require blocked with the exact recovery command.

## Architecture, audit and capacity addendum

1. Add a runtime @Auditable(action, resource) method annotation and Spring aspect
   for selected claim writes. Persist supplementary system-operation records in a
   dedicated append-only PostgreSQL table. Keep claim_audit unchanged as the
   domain transition history. Include action/resource/resource ID, authenticated
   actor, correlation ID, outcome, safe error type and timestamp. Do not serialize
   method arguments by default; never record credentials, tokens, claim documents,
   or unrestricted fact payloads. Successful audit insertion participates in the
   same transaction as the write, so an unaudited successful write cannot commit.
   A rejected operation may receive a separately committed failure record without
   replacing the original business error.
2. Idempotency applies to every mutating claim operation (create, facts update,
   human transition and system transition). Keys are scoped by authenticated actor
   and operation/resource; a matching key and request fingerprint returns the
   original result without repeating domain or system audit rows. Reusing a key
   with a different request returns a stable conflict. Concurrent identical
   requests produce one durable mutation and one effective audit event. Preserve
   the existing transition replay behavior.
3. Keep this as one modular Java/PostgreSQL service. Do not add Kafka, RabbitMQ,
   gRPC, external RPC or another broker. The existing database outbox remains the
   local durable mechanism for mock Challenge 14 effects.
4. Create architecture and workflow diagrams as image files under
   docs/architecture/images/, with editable source beside each exported image.
   Diagrams must match the implemented system and include the audit/idempotency
   path, PostgreSQL transaction boundary, local outbox, and configured claim states.
5. Add a generic capacity profile for 100 and 500 concurrent HTTP clients. Include
   reproducible JMeter plans, the required Compose setup/smoke sequence, dataset
   preparation, duration/ramp/think-time settings, error/latency/throughput
   measurements, resource monitoring, and report locations. Provide a clearly
   labeled starting hardware profile for each target; it is a planning estimate,
   not a measured service guarantee.
6. Keep JaCoCo gates at least 95% line and 90% branch with no business-code
   exclusions. Add meaningful tests for new audit/idempotency paths and rerun the
   gates until the added code satisfies them. Run Compose smoke after setup and
   execute the 100/500-client JMeter profiles only on an explicitly prepared test
   environment. Record actual test, coverage, smoke and load results; label runs
   that cannot be performed NOT_RUN with the exact command and reason.
7. Update OpenAPI, architecture/security/testing/operations docs, history,
   changelogs, requirement and delivery manifest. Do not claim capacity, SLA or
   performance until the corresponding load plan has actually run.

# Architecture

The planned service is one Spring Boot application with PostgreSQL. The YAML workflow is loaded into an immutable definition; named guard/effect strategies resolve configured identifiers. Claim use cases own transactions and coordinate MyBatis repository ports, domain audit, system-operation audit, idempotency receipts, payment records, and the local outbox. Mock effects dispatch after commit. Member-scoped list and count queries apply ownership filters in SQL.

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-claims-workflow-design.md` is the design baseline. T00 and the scoped T01 workflow engine are accepted after independent review. The engine is configuration-driven, resolves named guard/effect strategies, and produces pure effect intents. name: excalidraw-diagram
description: Create Excalidraw diagram JSON files that make visual arguments. Use when the user wants to visualize workflows, architectures, or concepts.
---

# Excalidraw Diagram Creator

Generate `.excalidraw` JSON files that **argue visually**, not just display information.

**Setup:** If the user asks you to set up this skill (renderer, dependencies, etc.), see `README.md` for instructions.

## Customization

**All colors and brand-specific styles live in one file:** `references/color-palette.md`. Read it before generating any diagram and use it as the single source of truth for all color choices — shape fills, strokes, text colors, evidence artifact backgrounds, everything.

To make this skill produce diagrams in your own brand style, edit `color-palette.md`. Everything else in this file is universal design methodology and Excalidraw best practices.

---

## Core Philosophy

**Diagrams should ARGUE, not DISPLAY.**

A diagram isn't formatted text. It's a visual argument that shows relationships, causality, and flow that words alone can't express. The shape should BE the meaning.

**The Isomorphism Test**: If you removed all text, would the structure alone communicate the concept? If not, redesign.

**The Education Test**: Could someone learn something concrete from this diagram, or does it just label boxes? A good diagram teaches—it shows actual formats, real event names, concrete examples.

---

## Depth Assessment (Do This First)

Before designing, determine what level of detail this diagram needs:

### Simple/Conceptual Diagrams
Use abstract shapes when:
- Explaining a mental model or philosophy
- The audience doesn't need technical specifics
- The concept IS the abstraction (e.g., "separation of concerns")

### Comprehensive/Technical Diagrams
Use concrete examples when:
- Diagramming a real system, protocol, or architecture
- The diagram will be used to teach or explain (e.g., YouTube video)
- The audience needs to understand what things actually look like
- You're showing how multiple technologies integrate

**For technical diagrams, you MUST include evidence artifacts** (see below).

---

## Research Mandate (For Technical Diagrams)

**Before drawing anything technical, research the actual specifications.**

If you're diagramming a protocol, API, or framework:
1. Look up the actual JSON/data formats
2. Find the real event names, method names, or API endpoints
3. Understand how the pieces actually connect
4. Use real terminology, not generic placeholders

Bad: "Protocol" → "Frontend"
Good: "AG-UI streams events (RUN_STARTED, STATE_DELTA, A2UI_UPDATE)" → "CopilotKit renders via createA2UIMessageRenderer()"

**Research makes diagrams accurate AND educational.**

---

## Evidence Artifacts

Evidence artifacts are concrete examples that prove your diagram is accurate and help viewers learn. Include them in technical diagrams.

**Types of evidence artifacts** (choose what's relevant to your diagram):

| Artifact Type | When to Use | How to Render |
|---------------|-------------|---------------|
| **Code snippets** | APIs, integrations, implementation details | Dark rectangle + syntax-colored text (see color palette for evidence artifact colors) |
| **Data/JSON examples** | Data formats, schemas, payloads | Dark rectangle + colored text (see color palette) |
| **Event/step sequences** | Protocols, workflows, lifecycles | Timeline pattern (line + dots + labels) |
| **UI mockups** | Showing actual output/results | Nested rectangles mimicking real UI |
| **Real input content** | Showing what goes IN to a system | Rectangle with sample content visible |
| **API/method names** | Real function calls, endpoints | Use actual names from docs, not placeholders |

**Example**: For a diagram about a streaming protocol, you might show:
- The actual event names from the spec (not just "Event 1", "Event 2")
- A code snippet showing how to connect
- What the streamed data actually looks like

**Example**: For a diagram about a data transformation pipeline:
- Show sample input data (actual format, not "Input")
- Show sample output data (actual format, not "Output")
- Show intermediate states if relevant

The key principle: **show what things actually look like**, not just what they're called.

---

## Multi-Zoom Architecture

Comprehensive diagrams operate at multiple zoom levels simultaneously. Think of it like a map that shows both the country borders AND the street names.

### Level 1: Summary Flow
A simplified overview showing the full pipeline or process at a glance. Often placed at the top or bottom of the diagram.

*Example*: `Input → Processing → Output` or `Client → Server → Database`

### Level 2: Section Boundaries
Labeled regions that group related components. These create visual "rooms" that help viewers understand what belongs together.

*Example*: Grouping by responsibility (Backend / Frontend), by phase (Setup / Execution / Cleanup), or by team (User / System / External)

### Level 3: Detail Inside Sections
Evidence artifacts, code snippets, and concrete examples within each section. This is where the educational value lives.

*Example*: Inside a "Backend" section, you might show the actual API response format, not just a box labeled "API Response"

**For comprehensive diagrams, aim to include all three levels.** The summary gives context, the sections organize, and the details teach.

### Bad vs Good

| Bad (Displaying) | Good (Arguing) |
|------------------|----------------|
| 5 equal boxes with labels | Each concept has a shape that mirrors its behavior |
| Card grid layout | Visual structure matches conceptual structure |
| Icons decorating text | Shapes that ARE the meaning |
| Same container for everything | Distinct visual vocabulary per concept |
| Everything in a box | Free-floating text with selective containers |

### Simple vs Comprehensive (Know Which You Need)

| Simple Diagram | Comprehensive Diagram |
|----------------|----…3121 tokens truncated…ionships. If A relates to B, there must be an arrow.

---

## Text Rules

**CRITICAL**: The JSON `text` property contains ONLY readable words.

```json
{
  "id": "myElement1",
  "text": "Start",
  "originalText": "Start"
}
```

Settings: `fontSize: 16`, `fontFamily: 3`, `textAlign: "center"`, `verticalAlign: "middle"`

---

## JSON Structure

```json
{
  "type": "excalidraw",
  "version": 2,
  "source": "https://excalidraw.com",
  "elements": [...],
  "appState": {
    "viewBackgroundColor": "#ffffff",
    "gridSize": 20
  },
  "files": {}
}
```

## Element Templates

See `references/element-templates.md` for copy-paste JSON templates for each element type (text, line, dot, rectangle, arrow). Pull colors from `references/color-palette.md` based on each element's semantic purpose.

---

## Render & Validate (MANDATORY)

You cannot judge a diagram from JSON alone. After generating or editing the Excalidraw JSON, you MUST render it to PNG, view the image, and fix what you see — in a loop until it's right. This is a core part of the workflow, not a final check.

### How to Render

```bash
cd .claude/skills/excalidraw-diagram/references && uv run python render_excalidraw.py <path-to-file.excalidraw>
```

This outputs a PNG next to the `.excalidraw` file. Then use the **Read tool** on the PNG to actually view it.

### The Loop

After generating the initial JSON, run this cycle:

**1. Render & View** — Run the render script, then Read the PNG.

**2. Audit against your original vision** — Before looking for bugs, compare the rendered result to what you designed in Steps 1-4. Ask:
- Does the visual structure match the conceptual structure you planned?
- Does each section use the pattern you intended (fan-out, convergence, timeline, etc.)?
- Does the eye flow through the diagram in the order you designed?
- Is the visual hierarchy correct — hero elements dominant, supporting elements smaller?
- For technical diagrams: are the evidence artifacts (code snippets, data examples) readable and properly placed?

**3. Check for visual defects:**
- Text clipped by or overflowing its container
- Text or shapes overlapping other elements
- Arrows crossing through elements instead of routing around them
- Arrows landing on the wrong element or pointing into empty space
- Labels floating ambiguously (not clearly anchored to what they describe)
- Uneven spacing between elements that should be evenly spaced
- Sections with too much whitespace next to sections that are too cramped
- Text too small to read at the rendered size
- Overall composition feels lopsided or unbalanced

**4. Fix** — Edit the JSON to address everything you found. Common fixes:
- Widen containers when text is clipped
- Adjust `x`/`y` coordinates to fix spacing and alignment
- Add intermediate waypoints to arrow `points` arrays to route around elements
- Reposition labels closer to the element they describe
- Resize elements to rebalance visual weight across sections

**5. Re-render & re-view** — Run the render script again and Read the new PNG.

**6. Repeat** — Keep cycling until the diagram passes both the vision check (Step 2) and the defect check (Step 3). Typically takes 2-4 iterations. Don't stop after one pass just because there are no critical bugs — if the composition could be better, improve it.

### When to Stop

The loop is done when:
- The rendered diagram matches the conceptual design from your planning steps
- No text is clipped, overlapping, or unreadable
- Arrows route cleanly and connect to the right elements
- Spacing is consistent and the composition is balanced
- You'd be comfortable showing it to someone without caveats

### First-Time Setup
If the render script hasn't been set up yet:
```bash
cd .claude/skills/excalidraw-diagram/references
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium
```

---

## Quality Checklist

### Depth & Evidence (Check First for Technical Diagrams)
1. **Research done**: Did you look up actual specs, formats, event names?
2. **Evidence artifacts**: Are there code snippets, JSON examples, or real data?
3. **Multi-zoom**: Does it have summary flow + section boundaries + detail?
4. **Concrete over abstract**: Real content shown, not just labeled boxes?
5. **Educational value**: Could someone learn something concrete from this?

### Conceptual
6. **Isomorphism**: Does each visual structure mirror its concept's behavior?
7. **Argument**: Does the diagram SHOW something text alone couldn't?
8. **Variety**: Does each major concept use a different visual pattern?
9. **No uniform containers**: Avoided card grids and equal boxes?

### Container Discipline
10. **Minimal containers**: Could any boxed element work as free-floating text instead?
11. **Lines as structure**: Are tree/timeline patterns using lines + text rather than boxes?
12. **Typography hierarchy**: Are font size and color creating visual hierarchy (reducing need for boxes)?

### Structural
13. **Connections**: Every relationship has an arrow or line
14. **Flow**: Clear visual path for the eye to follow
15. **Hierarchy**: Important elements are larger/more isolated

### Technical
16. **Text clean**: `text` contains only readable words
17. **Font**: `fontFamily: 3`
18. **Roughness**: `roughness: 0` for clean/modern (unless hand-drawn style requested)
19. **Opacity**: `opacity: 100` for all elements (no transparency)
20. **Container ratio**: <30% of text elements should be inside containers

### Visual Validation (Render Required)

# Color Palette & Brand Style

**This is the single source of truth for all colors and brand-specific styles.** To customize diagrams for your own brand, edit this file — everything else in the skill is universal.

---

## Shape Colors (Semantic)

Colors encode meaning, not decoration. Each semantic purpose has a fill/stroke pair.

| Semantic Purpose | Fill | Stroke |
|------------------|------|--------|
| Primary/Neutral | `#3b82f6` | `#1e3a5f` |
| Secondary | `#60a5fa` | `#1e3a5f` |
| Tertiary | `#93c5fd` | `#1e3a5f` |
| Start/Trigger | `#fed7aa` | `#c2410c` |
| End/Success | `#a7f3d0` | `#047857` |
| Warning/Reset | `#fee2e2` | `#dc2626` |
| Decision | `#fef3c7` | `#b45309` |
| AI/LLM | `#ddd6fe` | `#6d28d9` |
| Inactive/Disabled | `#dbeafe` | `#1e40af` (use dashed stroke) |
| Error | `#fecaca` | `#b91c1c` |

**Rule**: Always pair a darker stroke with a lighter fill for contrast.

---

## Text Colors (Hierarchy)

Use color on free-floating text to create visual hierarchy without containers.

| Level | Color | Use For |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Title | `#1e40af` | Section headings, major labels |
| Subtitle | `#3b82f6` | Subheadings, secondary labels |
| Body/Detail | `#64748b` | Descriptions, annotations, metadata |
| On light fills | `#374151` | Text inside light-colored shapes |
| On dark fills | `#ffffff` | Text inside dark-colored shapes |

---

## Evidence Artifact Colors

Used for code snippets, data examples, and other concrete evidence inside technical diagrams.

| Artifact | Background | Text Color |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Code snippet | `#1e293b` | Syntax-colored (language-appropriate) |
| JSON/data example | `#1e293b` | `#22c55e` (green) |

---

## Default Stroke & Line Colors

| Element | Color |
|---------|-------|
| Arrows | Use the stroke color of the source element's semantic purpose |
| Structural lines (dividers, trees, timelines) | Primary stroke (`#1e3a5f`) or Slate (`#64748b`) |
| Marker dots (fill + stroke) | Primary fill (`#3b82f6`) |

---

## Background

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Canvas background | `#ffffff` |

+# Architecture
+
+The application is one Spring Boot 3.5.16 service with MyBatis and PostgreSQL 16. The YAML workflow is loaded into an immutable definition; named guard/effect strategies resolve configured identifiers. REST maps only authenticated principals to domain actors. Claim use cases own transactions and coordinate the claim row, claim transition audit, supplementary system-operation audit, idempotency receipt, payment request and local outbox.
+
+## Transaction and effects
+
+Every mutation obtains a transaction-scoped advisory lock for `(actor, scope, idempotency key)`, checks its canonical request fingerprint, locks the claim row, validates expected version and workflow guards, and writes the updated claim plus all success evidence in one transaction. A retry with the same fingerprint returns its receipt; key reuse with another fingerprint conflicts. The database also enforces a unique receipt key, version checks, append-only audit triggers, and runtime-role column grants. A rejected operation may append a safe failure record through `REQUIRES_NEW` after its business transaction rolls back.
+
+An approved claim writes a payment request in the mutation transaction. The configured payment trigger creates a local outbox row in that same transaction. A scheduled dispatcher leases due rows, invokes mock delivery after the original commit, confirms a payment reference, and records delivery or a retry time. No external broker is part of this design.
+
+## API and observability
+
+The API is rooted at `/api/v1`. Claim and audit collections use zero-based `page` (default 0), `size` (default 20, maximum 100), deterministic ordering, and typed count/page responses. +# Security design and verification
+
+## Identity and authorization
+
+The service uses HTTP Basic with server-side session-backed CSRF protection. The browser fetches a CSRF token before mutation. A domain `Actor` is derived only from the authenticated principal and authorities; request bodies cannot select roles or member identity. The `system` principal must have the protected system authority and is accepted only by the system-transition endpoint. Human mutation methods reject the system identity. Member-scoped claim reads and audit access apply ownership checks, and list/count SQL includes member scope. Runtime database credentials have narrower grants than the Liquibase schema owner.
+
+The in-memory accounts (`clerk`, `lead`, `assessor`, `finance`, `member-demo`, `system`) are local Challenge 14 demonstration identities, not an enterprise identity provider. TLS termination, external identity, secret rotation, and production account provisioning are not included in this implementation.
+
+## Request and data controls
+
+- JSON parsing rejects unknown fields; JSON request bodies are capped at 65,536 bytes, including requests without a declared content length.
+- `X-Correlation-ID` accepts only 1–128 safe ASCII characters. Invalid/missing values get a generated UUID. The exact effective value flows through response, logs, and mutation audit.

+- Claim rows, immutable audit records, runtime grants and payment/outbox update columns are constrained in PostgreSQL. Domain audit and system-operation audit use append-only mutation triggers.
+- Error responses use stable API codes and avoid returning internal SQL or exception details. Failure audit stores the error type, not request bodies, credentials, documents, or unrestricted facts.
+
+## Security verification status
+
+Actor identity derivation, correlation handling, request-size enforcement, and request/resource contract rules have unit coverage. The controller regression verifies that writes use the filter's effective correlation value. Coordinator: gpt-6.1-sol / medium. Every implementation and review subagent:
gpt-6-luna / medium. Use at most three concurrent subagents outside the coordinator,

## Requirement loop

1. Read rules/REQUIREMENT.md, applicable rules, current docs/history and authoritative
   memory progress. For **each** new human message, append the verbatim prompt to
   `docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` and a dated requirement-change entry to
   `rules/REQUIREMENT.md` **before** implementation, even for follow-up requests.
   Establish append-only interaction evidence recording before dispatch. Enforce
   full pre-dispatch request capture for directly managed/model API calls; for
   host-managed calls preserve accessible task packets and execution evidence
   and document any unavailable raw payloads as NOT_CAPTURED.
2. Update acceptance criteria, to-do/DAG, inputs/outputs, exclusive patch paths,
   required checks and estimate. Freeze/compile shared interfaces before consumers.
3. For directly controlled LLM API invocations (including workers, reviewers and
   retries), persist the actual outbound request before dispatch and the inbound
   response/error/partial output afterward; fail closed if pre-dispatch request
   logging is unavailable. For host-managed coordinator/worker/reviewer calls,

4. Workers read source and draft candidate.patch plus handoff.json in their own
   artifact directory. They do not modify source, plans, memory or build output,
   run builds/Docker/DB/Git mutations, or spawn other agents.
5. Coordinator checks patch target ownership, base/contract hashes and full content,

6. Coordinator runs focused checks, captures command/exit code/source hash/report,
   prints test progress and fixes core causes through the owning worker.
7. A fresh independent reviewer inspects actual source/assertions/results and
   reports criteria coverage and actionable findings with file:line. Resolve

8. Coordinator verifies interaction evidence and independent-review trace links,

   `PARTIAL` alone does not prohibit implementation acceptance, provided mandatory

## One source writer

Workers write only rules/workflow/artifacts/TASK/ATTEMPT/. allowed_paths in the manifest
constrain the intended patch targets, not direct filesystem edits. Coordinator
owns source/shared files and serializes builds, database and Docker operations.
Independent task paths cannot overlap or contain one another. Shared ports,
pom/application YAML/changelog/manifest/memory changes go through the coordinator.

```bash
python3 scripts/workflow/verify_workflow.py --patch T01 rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
git apply --check rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
git apply rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
```

The host apply-patch tool can integrate validated text changes if git apply is
unavailable. Path checks do not review code behavior; content review remains
required. Single-writer integration prevents source/build write races; contract
and integration tests address semantic conflicts. Agent instructions are a
protocol, not an independently enforced filesystem sandbox.

planned → running → submitted → in_review → accepted. Failures require rework;
unavailable prerequisites require blocked with the exact recovery command.
Every attempt gets a new artifact directory; old and new attempts never run
concurrently. After repeated failures, repair the contract/task decomposition
while preserving the user's model choice. Do not silently change models.

Verification evidence needs command, exit_code0, source_hash and artifact. Review
evidence includes reviewer_agent distinct from author; coordinator approval is

# Architecture

The application is one Spring Boot 3.5.16 service with MyBatis and PostgreSQL 16. The YAML workflow is loaded into an immutable definition; named guard/effect strategies resolve configured identifiers. REST maps only authenticated principals to domain actors. Claim use cases own transactions and coordinate the claim row, claim transition audit, supplementary system-operation audit, idempotency receipt, payment request and local outbox.

## Transaction and effects

Every mutation obtains a transaction-scoped advisory lock for `(actor, scope, idempotency key)`, checks its canonical request fingerprint, locks the claim row, validates expected version and workflow guards, and writes the updated claim plus all success evidence in one transaction. A retry with the same fingerprint returns its receipt; key reuse with another fingerprint conflicts. The database also enforces a unique receipt key, version checks, append-only audit triggers, and runtime-role column grants. A rejected operation may append a safe failure record through `REQUIRES_NEW` after its business transaction rolls back.

An approved claim writes a payment request in the mutation transaction. The configured payment trigger creates a local outbox row in that same transaction. A scheduled dispatcher leases due rows, invokes mock delivery after the original commit, confirms a payment reference, and records delivery or a retry time. No external broker is part of this design.

## API and observability

The API is rooted at `/api/v1`. Claim and audit collections use zero-based `page` (default 0), `size` (default 20, maximum 100), deterministic ordering, and typed count/page responses. Member ownership filtering remains in SQL. `X-Correlation-ID` accepts only bounded safe ASCII, otherwise receives a generated UUID; the same effective value is returned, logged, and passed to mutation audit. It is kept separate from Micrometer observation trace/span context. Actuator health is public with hidden details; other actuator routes, including Prometheus, require authentication.

# Claims Workflow Orchestrator

A Java 21 / Spring Boot service for configuration-driven claim workflows. The application stores claims, transition and system audit records, idempotency receipts, payment requests, and payment outbox events in PostgreSQL through MyBatis and Liquibase.

- YAML-defined claim states, transitions, guards, roles, and effect plans.

# Quality gates

Task state is not test evidence. A worker submission becomes accepted only after
coordinator-run checks, independent review and source-matched acceptance records.

## Architecture and review

- State Machine: configured string states/edges; demonstrate a config-only addition.
- Strategy/Factory: guard/effect registries resolve supported capabilities and reject unknown IDs.
- SRP/DIP/ISP: pure engine, transactional application, small repository ports and MyBatis adapters.
- Immutable values: defensive nested facts and canonical PostgreSQL timestamp precision.
- Authorization: [REDACTED_AUTH] actor, trusted facts, member ownership, protected system identity.
- Consistency: atomic state/audit/payment/receipt/outbox, row lock/CAS, idempotent replay.
- Audit: runtime append/read only, trigger defense, no cascading deletion.
- Reliability: after-commit mock effects, retry state, no false exactly-once claim.
- Observability: real trace/span context, outcome/latency fields, no secret/medical-content logging.
- UI: dynamic states/choices, accessible forms/focus, responsive layout, escaping and clear errors.

## Acceptance cases

- C14-01: YAML loads eight initial states and nine edges with expected role/guard/effect metadata.
- C14-02: Happy path closes with five successful transition audit entries.
- C14-03: Rejection path includes reason/appeal instructions and eligible system closure.
- C14-04: Information loop resets assessment timer and clears stale completion before approval.
- C14-05: Illegal SUBMITTED-to-APPROVED edge reports source, target and available choices.
- C14-06: Unauthorized role fails at engine/application boundary without state/audit/outbox mutation.
- C14-07: Missing or invalid required documents fail with specific guard details.
- C14-08: Assessment cannot start without assigned assessor.
- C14-09: Incomplete report cannot approve/reject.
- C14-10: Amount equals limit passes; excess/negative/null/invalid currency fails appropriately.
- C14-11: Rejection and information request require nonblank reason/description.
- C14-12: Old information receipt fails; fresh server-stamped receipt permits return.
- C14-13: Payment initiation needs persisted request; closure needs confirmation/reference.
- C14-14: Appeal expiry boundary and member acknowledgement paths behave deterministically.
- C14-15: Three information requests succeed; fourth has exact escalation message; claims are independent.
- C14-16: Audit fields/order/claim scoping remain accurate and complete.
- C14-17: Runtime audit UPDATE/DELETE denied; owner trigger protects accidental mutation; no cascade.
- C14-18: Audit/outbox failure rolls back state, counter and payment request.
- C14-19: Rollback dispatches nothing; after-commit failure retains observable retry.
- C14-20: Concurrent same-version commands have one winner and no duplicate audit/payment.
- C14-21: Same actor/claim/key/payload replays result; different payload conflicts.
- C14-22: New state/edge works with configuration-only diff and dynamic interface options.
- C14-23: Duplicate/dangling/unknown guard/effect configuration fails startup clearly.
- C14-24: Terminal state has no outgoing choices.
- C14-25: HTTP401/403, ownership and system-role spoof protection.
- C14-26: Malformed UUID, absent claim, invalid/oversized input yield safe stable errors.
- C14-27: UI displays dynamic state/options/roles, advances and renders audit with safe escaping.
- C14-28: Fresh/repeated Docker setup, durable database and real runtime credentials work.
- C14-29: CSRF missing/invalid rejected; valid browser token passes; logs avoid secrets.

## Test execution and evidence

At least15 meaningful Java tests are required by the brief. Unit tests use JUnit5,
Mockito/AssertJ as appropriate. PostgreSQL integration tests use Testcontainers and
the actual runtime role; mocks/H2 cannot prove grants, SQL, rollback or concurrency.
Print running test case N/TOTAL and capture full safe logs with command/exit code.

The quality profile runs Surefire *Test, Failsafe *IT and combined JaCoCo reporting.
Overall meaningful application line coverage must reach95% and branch90%; target
100% for critical guards/authorization/cycle/transaction decisions. Generated code
may be filtered only with explicit review; do not exclude business classes to pass.
Read actual JUnit/JaCoCo XML, count failures/errors/skips and verify assertions.

```bash
mvn -B -Pquality clean verify
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker/compose.yml config --quiet
bash scripts/setup.sh
bash scripts/smoke.sh
bash scripts/run-scenarios.sh
```

Setup provisions only; tests are separate. Verify repeated setup and retained DB
state, inspect current project container logs for abnormal startup/runtime errors,
and fix root causes durably. Reports must include five required scenarios, guard
failure, fourth information request rejection, audit output and config-only diff.
Tie results to final source hashes. Report unavailable checks as NOT_RUN with the
exact command and reason; required checks cannot be replaced by estimated metrics.
Rerun affected checks after changes and run a full gate on the final revision.
"}

# Requirement and reference scope

## Governing scope

Implement the single Challenge 14 Claims Workflow Orchestrator defined in
`requirements/AI_Challenge_14.md`, `rules/REQUIREMENT.md`, and the current
`CHANGE_REQUEST.md`. Keep the approved Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5.16, MyBatis

## Exclusions

The change request is a format and process template, not authorization to import
unrelated messaging platforms, separate microservice topologies, alternate
languages, migrations, or business domains. The supplied Java reference's
reusable engineering practices apply within this one claims application; Kafka,
RabbitMQ, gRPC, Redis, JWT, JPA, Flyway, and additional deployable services remain
out of scope under the current requirements.

# Challenge 14 implementation contracts

## Runtime boundary

- One Spring Boot 3.5.16 / Java 21 service, PostgreSQL 16, MyBatis 3.0.5 and Liquibase.
- Standard resource layout: `classpath:db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yml`; mapper XML at `classpath:sql/service/claim/*.xml`; workflow YAML at `classpath:config/workflow.yml`.
- Runtime JDBC role defaults to `claims_runtime`; Liquibase role defaults to `claims_migration`. Compose must provision separate credentials. Never embed a usable secret in source or templates.
- HTTP API base is `/api/v1`; authentication uses HTTP Basic for the local Challenge 14 environment. Human demo identities are `clerk`, `lead`, `assessor`, `finance`, and `member-<memberId>`; workflow roles are derived from the authenticated principal. - Browser state-changing requests require a valid CSRF token. Actuator health is public with details hidden; other actuator endpoints, including Prometheus, require authentication.

## Frozen service/API types

`ClaimUseCases` is the application boundary. It accepts only domain commands and `Actor`, never HTTP request DTOs:

```java
Claim create(CreateClaimCommand command, Actor actor, String idempotencyKey, String correlationId);
```

class HttpClient:
    def __init__(self, username=None, password=[REDACTED_SECRET]
        self.cookies = http.cookiejar.CookieJar()
        self.opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(self.cookies))
        self.auth = None
        self.csrf_header = None
        self.csrf_token = None
        if username is not None:
            encoded = base64.b64encode(f"{username}:{password}".encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")
            self.auth = f"Basic {encoded}"
            status, body, _ = self.request("GET", "/api/session")
            require(status == 200, f"{username} session returned HTTP {status}")
            require(bool(body.get("csrfToken")) and bool(body.get("csrfHeader")), "session has no CSRF material")
            self.csrf_token = body["csrfToken"]
            self.csrf_header = body["csrfHeader"]

    def request(self, method, path, body=None, include_auth=True, include_csrf=True):
        headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
        if include_auth and self.auth:
            headers["Authorization"] = self.auth
        raw = None
        if body is not None:
            raw = json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        if method not in ("GET", "HEAD") and include_csrf and self.csrf_token:
            headers[self.csrf_header] = self.csrf_token
        request = urllib.request.Request(base_url + path, data=raw, headers=headers, method=method)
        try:
            with self.opener.open(request, timeout=20) as response:
                content = response.read()
                parsed = json.loads(content) if content else {}
                return response.status, parsed, dict(response.headers)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            content = error.read()
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(content) if content else {}
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                parsed = {"body": "<non-json error body>"}
            return error.code, parsed, dict(error.headers)
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as error:
            raise ScenarioFailure(f"request to {path} failed: {type(error).__name__}") from None

def create(client, member="member-001"):

def patch_facts(client, claim, updates):

        "expectedVersion": claim["version"], "updates": updates,

def command(client, claim, target, key=None, notes="acceptance scenario"):
    body = {
        "target": target,
        "expectedVersion": claim["version"],
        "idempotencyKey": key or str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "notes": notes,

def system_close(client, claim):
    return client.request("POST", f"/api/system/claims/{claim['id']}/close", {
        "expectedVersion": claim["version"],

def audit(client, claim):
    status, rows, _ = client.request("GET", f"/api/claims/{claim['id']}/audit")
    require(status == 200, f"audit read returned HTTP {status}")
    return rows

def assert_audit_path(rows, expected_states):
    observed = [entry["toState"] for entry in rows]
    require(observed == expected_states, f"audit states differ: {observed}")
    sequences = [entry["sequence"] for entry in rows]
    require(all(a < b for a, b in zip(sequences, sequences[1:])), "audit sequence is not strictly increasing")

def assert_unchanged(client, claim, before):
    after = audit(client, claim)
    require(after == before, "failed operation changed the audit log")
    return after

def export(name, claim, rows, outcomes):
    path = output_dir / f"{name}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps({
        "scenario": name,
        "claim": claim,
        "audit": rows,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
    }, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

def patch_ok(client, claim, updates, description):
    status, updated, _ = patch_facts(client, claim, updates)
    require(status == 200, f"{description} facts update returned HTTP {status}")
    return updated

def transition_ok(client, claim, target, description):
    status, updated, _ = command(client, claim, target)
    require(status == 200 and updated.get("state") == target,
            f"{description} transition returned HTTP {status}")
    return updated

info:
  title: Claims Workflow API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Secured single-service claims workflow API. Correlation IDs use X-Correlation-ID and are separate from tracing identifiers.
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:8080/api/v1
security:
  - basicAuth: []
paths:
  /claims:
    get:
      summary: List visible claims
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Page'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Size'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Paged claims visible to the authenticated actor
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ClaimPage' }
        '401': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
    post:
      summary: Create a claim
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateClaimRequest' }
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Claim created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Claim' }
        '409': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    get:
      summary: Get a claim
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Claim details
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Claim' }
        '404': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}/facts:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    put:
      summary: Replace permitted claim facts
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/UpdateFactsRequest' }
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Updated claim
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Claim' }
        '409': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}/transitions:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    get:
      summary: List configured transitions and current guard/role availability
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Configured transitions for the claim's current state
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { type: array, items: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/WorkflowOption' } }
    post:
      summary: Execute a human-authorized configured transition
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/TransitionRequest' }
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Transition outcome containing the resulting claim, audit record, and replay status
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/TransitionResult' }
        '409': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}/rejection-acknowledgement:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    post:
      summary: Acknowledge a rejected claim as its owner member
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/AcknowledgeRejectionRequest' }
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Versioned claim with server-stamped acknowledgment
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Claim' }
        '403': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
        '409': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}/system-transitions:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    post:
      summary: Execute a protected system transition
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/TransitionRequest' }
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Transition outcome containing the resulting claim, audit record, and replay status
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/TransitionResult' }
        '403': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Error' }
  /claims/{claimId}/audit:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClaimId'
    get:
      summary: Read paged immutable claim transition history
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Page'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Size'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/CorrelationId'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Ordered audit history
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/AuditPage' }
components:
  securitySchemes:
    basicAuth: { type: http, scheme: basic }
  parameters:
    Page:
      name: page
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, minimum: 0, default: 0 }
    Size:
      name: size
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20 }
    CorrelationId:
      name: X-Correlation-ID
      in: header
