      name: Idempotency-Key
      in: header
      required: true
      schema: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 128 }
    ClaimId:
      name: claimId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: { type: string, format: uuid }
  schemas:
    PageMetadata:
      type: object
      required: [items, total, page, size, totalPages]
      properties:
        items: { type: array, items: {} }
        total: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        page: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
        size: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100 }
        totalPages: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
    ClaimPage:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/PageMetadata'
        - type: object
          properties:
            items: { type: array, items: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Claim' } }
    AuditPage:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/PageMetadata'
        - type: object
          properties:
            items: { type: array, items: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/AuditEntry' } }
    Claim:
      type: object
      required: [id, state, policyLimit, currency, version, facts, createdAt, updatedAt]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, format: uuid }
        state: { type: string }
        policyLimit: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 9999999999999999.99, multipleOf: 0.01 }
        currency: { type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3}$' }
        version: { type: integer, format: int64 }
        facts: { type: object, additionalProperties: true }
        createdAt: { type: string, format: date-time }
        updatedAt: { type: string, format: date-time }
    AuditEntry:
      type: object
      required: [id, sequence, timestamp, toState, actorId, role, reason, correlationId]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, format: uuid }
        sequence: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 0 }
        timestamp: { type: string, format: date-time }
        fromState: { type: string }
        toState: { type: string }
        actorId: { type: string }
        role: { type: string }
        reason: { type: string }
        correlationId: { type: string }
    CreateClaimRequest:
      type: object
      required: [policyLimit, currency, facts]
      properties:
        policyLimit: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 9999999999999999.99, multipleOf: 0.01 }
        currency: { type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3}$' }
        facts: { type: object, maxProperties: 100, additionalProperties: true }
    UpdateFactsRequest:
      type: object
      required: [expectedVersion, facts]
package com.papaya.claims.security;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.security.config.Customizer;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configuration.EnableWebSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.http.SessionCreationPolicy;
import org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.factory.PasswordEncoderFactories;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.provisioning.InMemoryUserDetailsManager;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;

@Configuration
@EnableWebSecurity
public class SecurityConfiguration {
    @Bean
    PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() { return PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder(); }

    @Bean
    InMemoryUserDetailsManager users(PasswordEncoder encoder,
            @Value("${claims.security.demo-password:}") String humanPassword,
            @Value("${claims.security.system-password:}") String systemPassword) {
        requireConfiguredSecret(humanPassword, "CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD");
        requireConfiguredSecret(systemPassword, "CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD");
        return new InMemoryUserDetailsManager(
                User.withUsername("clerk").password(encoder.encode(humanPassword)).roles("DOCUMENT_CLERK").build(),
                User.withUsername("lead").password(encoder.encode(humanPassword)).roles("TEAM_LEAD").build(),
                User.withUsername("assessor").password(encoder.encode(humanPassword)).roles("ASSESSOR").build(),
                User.withUsername("finance").password(encoder.encode(humanPassword)).roles("FINANCE").build(),
                User.withUsername("member-demo").password(encoder.encode(humanPassword)).roles("MEMBER").build(),
                User.withUsername("system").password(encoder.encode(systemPassword)).roles("SYSTEM").build());
    }

    @Bean
    SecurityFilterChain security(HttpSecurity http, ObjectMapper json) throws Exception {
        return http
                .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                        .requestMatchers("/", "/index.html", "/styles.css", "/app.js", "/favicon.ico", "/actuator/health", "/v3/api-docs/**", "/swagger-ui/**").permitAll()
                        .anyRequest().authenticated())
                .httpBasic(Customizer.withDefaults())
                .csrf(Customizer.withDefaults())
                .exceptionHandling(errors -> errors.authenticationEntryPoint(new JsonSecurityHandlers(json))
                        .accessDeniedHandler(new JsonSecurityHandlers(json)))
                .sessionManagement(session -> session.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.IF_REQUIRED))
                .build();
    }

    private static void requireConfiguredSecret(String value, String name) {
        if (value == null || value.isBlank() || value.startsWith("CHANGE_ME_"))
            throw new IllegalStateException(name + " must be configured to start the application");
    }
}

    confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,

);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exercise the authenticated HTTP claim lifecycle without printing credentials or payloads."""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import http.cookiejar
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path


def read_env(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    values: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        values[key.strip()] = value.strip()
    return values


class Api:
    def __init__(self, base: str, passwords: dict[str, str]):
        self.base = base.rstrip("/")
        self.passwords = passwords
        self.cookies = http.cookiejar.CookieJar()
        self.opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(self.cookies))

    def call(self, username: str | None, method: str, path: str, *, body=None, key=None, csrf=None):
        headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
        if body is not None:
            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        if key:
            headers["Idempotency-Key"] = key
        if csrf:
            headers[csrf["csrfHeaderName"]] = csrf["csrfToken"]
        if username:
            auth = base64.b64encode(f"{username}:{self.passwords[username]}".encode()).decode()
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Basic {auth}"
        data = json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")).encode() if body is not None else None
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
        try:
            with self.opener.open(request, timeout=10) as response:
                content = response.read()
                return response.status, json.loads(content) if content else None, response.headers
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            content = error.read()
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(content) if content else None
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                parsed = None
            return error.code, parsed, error.headers


def main() -> int:
    env_path = Path(os.environ.get("CLAIMS_ENV_FILE", ".env"))
    if not env_path.is_file():
        print("Missing .env; run bash scripts/setup.sh first.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    env = read_env(env_path)
    required = ("CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD", "CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD")
    if any(not env.get(name) or env[name].startswith("CHANGE_ME_") for name in required):
        print("Configured credentials are missing or still placeholders.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    port = env.get("SERVER_PORT", "8080")
    api = Api(os.environ.get("CLAIMS_API_BASE", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"), {
        "clerk": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "lead": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"],
        "assessor": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "finance": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"],
        "member-demo": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "system": env["CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD"],
    })
    total = 20
    case = 0

    def check(name: str, actual: int, expected: int) -> None:
        nonlocal case
        case += 1
        print(f"running test case {case}/{total}: {name}")
        if actual != expected:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: expected HTTP {expected}, received HTTP {actual}")

    try:
        status, _, _ = api.call(None, "GET", "/api/v1/claims?page=0&size=1")
        check("unauthenticated claims request is rejected", status, 401)

        status, csrf, _ = api.call("clerk", "GET", "/api/v1/session")
        check("authenticated session supplies CSRF token", status, 200)
        if not all(csrf.get(field) for field in ("csrfHeaderName", "csrfParameterName", "csrfToken")):
            raise RuntimeError("session did not return the expected CSRF contract")

        status, created, headers = api.call("member-demo", "POST", "/api/v1/claims", key="e2e-create-1",
            csrf=csrf, body={"policyLimit": 500, "currency": "USD", "facts": {"requestedAmount": 125.50}})
        check("member creates claim", status, 201)
        claim_id = created["id"]
        if headers.get("Location", "").endswith(claim_id) is False:
            raise RuntimeError("create response Location does not identify the returned claim")

        status, replay, _ = api.call("member-demo", "POST", "/api/v1/claims", key="e2e-create-1",
            csrf=csrf, body={"policyLimit": 500, "currency": "USD", "facts": {"requestedAmount": 125.50}})
        check("create idempotency replays the original claim", status, 201)
        if replay["id"] != claim_id:
            raise RuntimeError("idempotent create returned a different claim id")

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}")
        check("claim owner can read claim", status, 200)
        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/audit")
        check("claim owner can read audit", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key="e2e-no-csrf", body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {}}})
        check("unsafe request without CSRF token is rejected", status, 403)

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key="e2e-member-write-denied", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {"invoice": {"present": True}}}})
        check("member cannot edit submitted document roster", status, 403)

        status, _, _ = api.call("clerk", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key="e2e-documents", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {"invoice": {"required": True, "present": True, "valid": True}}}})
        check("document clerk records complete document", status, 200)

        status, transitioned, _ = api.call("clerk", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key="e2e-verify", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED", "expectedVersion": 1, "reason": "Documents verified", "facts": {}})
        check("document clerk verifies claim", status, 200)
        if transitioned["claim"]["version"] != 2:
            raise RuntimeError("document verification did not advance the claim version")

        status, _, _ = api.call("lead", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key="e2e-assign", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 2, "facts": {"assessorId": "assessor"}})
        check("team lead assigns assessor", status, 200)

        status, started, _ = api.call("lead", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key="e2e-start-assessment", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "UNDER_ASSESSMENT", "expectedVersion": 3, "reason": "Assigned", "facts": {}})
        check("team lead starts assessment", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("assessor", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key="e2e-report", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 4, "facts": {"assessmentReport": {"complete": True}}})
        check("assigned assessor submits report", status, 200)

        status, approved, _ = api.call("assessor", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key="e2e-approve", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "APPROVED", "expectedVersion": 5, "reason": "Covered", "facts": {}})
        check("assessor approves and persists payment request", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("finance", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key="e2e-initiate-payment", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "PAYMENT_INITIATED", "expectedVersion": 6, "reason": "Dispatch", "facts": {}})
        check("finance dispatches payment via outbox", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("assessor", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/system-transitions",
            key="e2e-forbidden-system", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "CLOSED", "expectedVersion": 7, "reason": "forbidden", "facts": {}})
        check("human identity cannot invoke system transition", status, 403)

        status, options, _ = api.call("finance", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions")
        check("finance can inspect transition options", status, 200)
        close_available = next((option.get("available", False) for option in options
                                if option.get("transitionId") == "close-paid-claim"), False)
        attempts = 0
        while not close_available and attempts < 30:
            time.sleep(1)
            status, options, _ = api.call("finance", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions")
            if status != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(f"payment confirmation poll returned HTTP {status}")
            close_available = next((option.get("available", False) for option in options
                                    if option.get("transitionId") == "close-paid-claim"), False)
            attempts += 1
        if not close_available:
            raise RuntimeError("payment outbox did not confirm within 30 seconds")
        status, closed, _ = api.call("finance", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key="e2e-close-paid", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "CLOSED", "expectedVersion": 7, "reason": "Payment confirmed", "facts": {}})
        check("finance closes claim after outbox confirmation", status, 200)
        if closed["claim"]["state"] != "CLOSED":
            raise RuntimeError("claim did not reach CLOSED")

        status, claim_list, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", "/api/v1/claims?page=0&size=20")
        check("member list endpoint returns visible claims", status, 200)
        if not any(item["id"] == claim_id for item in claim_list["items"]):
            raise RuntimeError("created claim is absent from the member-visible list")

        status, audit, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/audit")
        check("complete lifecycle exposes claim transition audit", status, 200)
        if len(audit["items"]) < 5:
            raise RuntimeError("expected transition audit records were not persisted")
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as error:
        print(f"Scenario failure after {case}/{total} cases: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Completed {case}/{total} end-to-end API scenarios.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Quality gates

Task state is not test evidence. A worker submission becomes accepted only after
coordinator-run checks, independent review and source-matched acceptance records.

## Architecture and review

- State Machine: configured string states/edges; demonstrate a config-only addition.
- Strategy/Factory: guard/effect registries resolve supported capabilities and reject unknown IDs.
- SRP/DIP/ISP: pure engine, transactional application, small repository ports and MyBatis adapters.
- Immutable values: defensive nested facts and canonical PostgreSQL timestamp precision.
- Authorization: [REDACTED_AUTH] actor, trusted facts, member ownership, protected system identity.
- Consistency: atomic state/audit/payment/receipt/outbox, row lock/CAS, idempotent replay.
- Audit: runtime append/read only, trigger defense, no cascading deletion.
- Reliability: after-commit mock effects, retry state, no false exactly-once claim.
- Observability: real trace/span context, outcome/latency fields, no secret/medical-content logging.
- UI: dynamic states/choices, accessible forms/focus, responsive layout, escaping and clear errors.

## Acceptance cases

- C14-01: YAML loads eight initial states and nine edges with expected role/guard/effect metadata.
- C14-02: Happy path closes with five successful transition audit entries.
- C14-03: Rejection path includes reason/appeal instructions and eligible system closure.
- C14-04: Information loop resets assessment timer and clears stale completion before approval.
- C14-05: Illegal SUBMITTED-to-APPROVED edge reports source, target and available choices.
- C14-06: Unauthorized role fails at engine/application boundary without state/audit/outbox mutation.
- C14-07: Missing or invalid required documents fail with specific guard details.
- C14-08: Assessment cannot start without assigned assessor.
- C14-09: Incomplete report cannot approve/reject.
- C14-10: Amount equals limit passes; excess/negative/null/invalid currency fails appropriately.
- C14-11: Rejection and information request require nonblank reason/description.
- C14-12: Old information receipt fails; fresh server-stamped receipt permits return.
- C14-13: Payment initiation needs persisted request; closure needs confirmation/reference.
- C14-14: Appeal expiry boundary and member acknowledgement paths behave deterministically.
- C14-15: Three information requests succeed; fourth has exact escalation message; claims are independent.
- C14-16: Audit fields/order/claim scoping remain accurate and complete.
- C14-17: Runtime audit UPDATE/DELETE denied; owner trigger protects accidental mutation; no cascade.
- C14-18: Audit/outbox failure rolls back state, counter and payment request.
- C14-19: Rollback dispatches nothing; after-commit failure retains observable retry.
- C14-20: Concurrent same-version commands have one winner and no duplicate audit/payment.
- C14-21: Same actor/claim/key/payload replays result; different payload conflicts.
- C14-22: New state/edge works with configuration-only diff and dynamic interface options.
- C14-23: Duplicate/dangling/unknown guard/effect configuration fails startup clearly.
- C14-24: Terminal state has no outgoing choices.
- C14-25: HTTP401/403, ownership and system-role spoof protection.
- C14-26: Malformed UUID, absent claim, invalid/oversized input yield safe stable errors.
- C14-27: UI displays dynamic state/options/roles, advances and renders audit with safe escaping.
- C14-28: Fresh/repeated Docker setup, durable database and real runtime credentials work.
- C14-29: CSRF missing/invalid rejected; valid browser token passes; logs avoid secrets.

## Test execution and evidence

At least15 meaningful Java tests are required by the brief. Unit tests use JUnit5,
Mockito/AssertJ as appropriate. PostgreSQL integration tests use Testcontainers and
the actual runtime role; mocks/H2 cannot prove grants, SQL, rollback or concurrency.
Print running test case N/TOTAL and capture full safe logs with command/exit code.

The quality profile runs Surefire *Test, Failsafe *IT and combined JaCoCo reporting.
Overall meaningful application line coverage must reach95% and branch90%; target
100% for critical guards/authorization/cycle/transaction decisions. Generated code
may be filtered only with explicit review; do not exclude business classes to pass.
Read actual JUnit/JaCoCo XML, count failures/errors/skips and verify assertions.

```bash
mvn -B -Pquality clean verify
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker/compose.yml config --quiet
bash scripts/setup.sh
bash scripts/smoke.sh
bash scripts/run-scenarios.sh
```

Setup provisions only; tests are separate. Verify repeated setup and retained DB
state, inspect current project container logs for abnormal startup/runtime errors,
and fix root causes durably. Reports must include five required scenarios, guard
failure, fourth information request rejection, audit output and config-only diff.
Tie results to final source hashes. Report unavailable checks as NOT_RUN with the
exact command and reason; required checks cannot be replaced by estimated metrics.
Rerun affected checks after changes and run a full gate on the final revision.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

env_file=.env
example=.env.example
if [[ ! -f "$env_file" ]]; then
  cp "$example" "$env_file"
  chmod 600 "$env_file"
fi

replace_dummy() {
  local key=$1 value
  value=$(awk -F= -v key="$key" '$1 == key { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; found=1; exit } END { if (!found) exit 1 }' "$env_file") || {
    echo "Missing $key in .env" >&2
    return 1
  }
  if [[ "$value" == CHANGE_ME_* || -z "$value" ]]; then
    value=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
    sed -i "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$env_file"
  fi
}

replace_dummy CLAIMS_BOOTSTRAP_DB_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD
replace_dummy CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD
chmod 600 "$env_file"

compose=(docker compose --env-file "$env_file" -f docker/compose.yml)
"${compose[@]}" config --quiet
"${compose[@]}" up -d --build --wait --wait-timeout 180
echo "Claims services are healthy. Run bash scripts/smoke.sh to verify the API."
services:
  database:
    image: postgres:16
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: claims
      POSTGRES_USER: claims_bootstrap
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: [REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_BOOTSTRAP_DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_USER: claims_migration
      CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] ${CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_USER: claims_runtime
      CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] ${CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - claims-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./initdb/10-runtime-role.sh:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/10-runtime-role.sh:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U \"$${POSTGRES_USER}\" -d \"$${POSTGRES_DB}\""]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 10s

  app:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      database:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      CLAIMS_DATABASE_URL: ${CLAIMS_DATABASE_URL:?Set CLAIMS_DATABASE_URL in .env}
      CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_USER: claims_runtime
      CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] ${CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_USER: claims_migration
      CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] ${CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_MIGRATION_DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      SERVER_PORT: 8080
      CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] ${CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD in .env}
      CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] ${CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD in .env}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${SERVER_PORT:-8080}:8080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 60s

# Architecture

The application is one Spring Boot 3.5.16 service with MyBatis and PostgreSQL 16. The YAML workflow is loaded into an immutable definition; named guard/effect strategies resolve configured identifiers. REST maps only authenticated principals to domain actors. Claim use cases own transactions and coordinate the claim row, claim transition audit, supplementary system-operation audit, idempotency receipt, payment request and local outbox.

## Transaction and effects

Every mutation obtains a transaction-scoped advisory lock for `(actor, scope, idempotency key)`, checks its canonical request fingerprint, locks the claim row, validates expected version and workflow guards, and writes the updated claim plus all success evidence in one transaction. A retry with the same fingerprint returns its receipt; key reuse with another fingerprint conflicts. The database also enforces a unique receipt key, version checks, append-only audit triggers, and runtime-role column grants. A rejected operation may append a safe failure record through `REQUIRES_NEW` after its business transaction rolls back.

An approved claim writes a payment request in the mutation transaction. The configured payment trigger creates a local outbox row in that same transaction. A scheduled dispatcher leases due rows, invokes mock delivery after the original commit, confirms a payment reference, and records delivery or a retry time. No external broker is part of this design.

## API and observability

The API is rooted at `/api/v1`. Claim and audit collections use zero-based `page` (default 0), `size` (default 20, maximum 100), deterministic ordering, and typed count/page responses. Member ownership filtering remains in SQL. `X-Correlation-ID` accepts only bounded safe ASCII, otherwise receives a generated UUID; the same effective value is returned, logged, and passed to mutation audit. # Security design and verification

## Identity and authorization

The service uses HTTP Basic with server-side session-backed CSRF protection. The browser fetches a CSRF token before mutation. A domain `Actor` is derived only from the authenticated principal and authorities; request bodies cannot select roles or member identity. The `system` principal must have the protected system authority and is accepted only by the system-transition endpoint. Human mutation methods reject the system identity. Member-scoped claim reads and audit access apply ownership checks, and list/count SQL includes member scope. Runtime database credentials have narrower grants than the Liquibase schema owner.

The in-memory accounts (`clerk`, `lead`, `assessor`, `finance`, `member-demo`, `system`) are local Challenge 14 demonstration identities, not an enterprise identity provider. Human and system passwords come from separate environment variables. Startup fails for empty or `CHANGE_ME_` passwords. Compose binds the HTTP port to loopback by default. TLS termination, external identity, secret rotation, and production account provisioning are not included in this implementation.

## Request and data controls

- JSON parsing rejects unknown fields; JSON request bodies are capped at 65,536 bytes, including requests without a declared content length.
- `X-Correlation-ID` accepts only 1–128 safe ASCII characters. Invalid/missing values get a generated UUID. The exact effective value flows through response, logs, and mutation audit.
- Every mutating claim operation requires an idempotency key; actor, operation/resource scope, canonical fingerprint and response are persisted transactionally.
- Claim rows, immutable audit records, runtime grants and payment/outbox update columns are constrained in PostgreSQL. Domain audit and system-operation audit use append-only mutation triggers.
- Error responses use stable API codes and avoid returning internal SQL or exception details. Failure audit stores the error type, not request bodies, credentials, documents, or unrestricted facts.

The controller regression verifies that writes use the filter's effective correlation value. Runtime HTTP authentication/authorization, CSRF, denied response envelopes, ownership isolation in PostgreSQL, audit immutability, and role grants require application/database execution and remain unverified because Docker socket access is denied. The current unit suite and static review are not a security certification.

# Coordinator and worker workflow

Coordinator: gpt-6.1-sol / medium. Every implementation and review subagent:
gpt-6-luna / medium. Use at most three concurrent subagents outside the coordinator,
subject to host limits. Pass explicit model/effort and fresh context when spawning.
Instructions alone do not change the active primary model or host permissions.

## Requirement loop

1. Read rules/REQUIREMENT.md, applicable rules, current docs/history and authoritative
   memory progress. For **each** new human message, append the verbatim prompt to
   `docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` and a dated requirement-change entry to
   `rules/REQUIREMENT.md` **before** implementation, even for follow-up requests.
   Establish append-only interaction evidence recording before dispatch. Enforce
   full pre-dispatch request capture for directly managed/model API calls; for
   host-managed calls preserve accessible task packets and execution evidence
   and document any unavailable raw payloads as NOT_CAPTURED.
2. Update acceptance criteria, to-do/DAG, inputs/outputs, exclusive patch paths,
   required checks and estimate. Freeze/compile shared interfaces before consumers.
3. For directly controlled LLM API invocations (including workers, reviewers and
   retries), persist the actual outbound request before dispatch and the inbound
   response/error/partial output afterward; fail closed if pre-dispatch request
   logging is unavailable. For host-managed coordinator/worker/reviewer calls,
   persist every exposed task packet, input/output, model/attempt metadata and
   review artifact. If the host hides raw model payloads, record the affected
   interaction ID, reason and `NOT_CAPTURED` fields, set audit status `PARTIAL`,
   and continue authorized dispatch (no fabrication or COMPLETE audit claim).
   Link interactions -> requirements -> tasks/attempts. Protect secrets, dispatch
   only when dependencies are accepted, and pass source/contract hashes, role
   and exclusive task/attempt artifact directory.
4. Workers read source and draft candidate.patch plus handoff.json in their own
   artifact directory. They do not modify source, plans, memory or build output,
   run builds/Docker/DB/Git mutations, or spawn other agents.
5. Coordinator checks patch target ownership, base/contract hashes and full content,
   dry-runs the patch and applies it serially. Rebase stale patches before apply.
6. Coordinator runs focused checks, captures command/exit code/source hash/report,
   prints test progress and fixes core causes through the owning worker.
7. A fresh independent reviewer inspects actual source/assertions/results and
   reports criteria coverage and actionable findings with file:line. Resolve
   correctness/security/requirement findings and rereview affected changes.
8. Coordinator verifies interaction evidence and independent-review trace links,
   recording missing host-managed payloads as `NOT_CAPTURED` and audit `PARTIAL`.
   `PARTIAL` alone does not prohibit implementation acceptance, provided mandatory
   tests pass, review is independent, source/evidence match, and no explicit full-
   capture acceptance condition remains unmet. Never report full traceability when
   any required payload is missing. Coordinator accepts only when
   every required command has final PASS/exit0 and other gates are satisfied. Update manifest,
   checklist, memory and synchronized history after acceptance.
9. Run final integrated gates/review, update current architecture/runbook/history,
   and prepare source/config/scenarios/audit/diff/raw-conversation submission.

## One source writer

Workers write only rules/workflow/artifacts/TASK/ATTEMPT/. allowed_paths in the manifest
constrain the intended patch targets, not direct filesystem edits. Coordinator
owns source/shared files and serializes builds, database and Docker operations.
Independent task paths cannot overlap or contain one another. Shared ports,
pom/application YAML/changelog/manifest/memory changes go through the coordinator.

Validate candidate scope before apply:

```bash
python3 scripts/workflow/verify_workflow.py --patch T01 rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
git apply --check rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
git apply rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
```

The host apply-patch tool can integrate validated text changes if git apply is
unavailable. Path checks do not review code behavior; content review remains
required. Single-writer integration prevents source/build write races; contract
and integration tests address semantic conflicts. Agent instructions are a
protocol, not an independently enforced filesystem sandbox.

## State, evidence and recovery

planned → running → submitted → in_review → accepted. Failures require rework;
unavailable prerequisites require blocked with the exact recovery command.
Every attempt gets a new artifact directory; old and new attempts never run
concurrently. After repeated failures, repair the contract/task decomposition
while preserving the user's model choice. Do not silently change models.

Verification evidence needs command, exit_code0, source_hash and artifact. Review
evidence includes reviewer_agent distinct from author; coordinator approval is
separate. All required commands need final PASS on the accepted source; NOT_RUN
cannot stand in for a pass. Final-review tasks compare reviewer against source
authors rather than requiring a review of the review itself. Validator checks
structure, not artifact signatures or full status history; coordinator reads
actual logs/files and checks runtime identity.

Only coordinator checkpoints shared memory before/after steps. Resume from
agent-memory resume, inspect active agents/leases/artifacts/base hashes, and
continue unfinished work. history/task_on_progress.md is a synchronized view;
.agent-memory/task_on_progress.md is authoritative. Update history changelog,
dated technical entries and docs/HISTORY.md after project updates.

Use TASK-PACKET.md, REVIEW-PACKET.md and QUALITY-GATES.md for dispatch/review.
# Quality gates

Task state is not test evidence. A worker submission becomes accepted only after
coordinator-run checks, independent review and source-matched acceptance records.

## Architecture and review

- State Machine: configured string states/edges; demonstrate a config-only addition.
- Strategy/Factory: guard/effect registries resolve supported capabilities and reject unknown IDs.
- SRP/DIP/ISP: pure engine, transactional application, small repository ports and MyBatis adapters.
- Immutable values: defensive nested facts and canonical PostgreSQL timestamp precision.
- Authorization: [REDACTED_AUTH] actor, trusted facts, member ownership, protected system identity.
- Consistency: atomic state/audit/payment/receipt/outbox, row lock/CAS, idempotent replay.
- Audit: runtime append/read only, trigger defense, no cascading deletion.
- Reliability: after-commit mock effects, retry state, no false exactly-once claim.
- Observability: real trace/span context, outcome/latency fields, no secret/medical-content logging.
- UI: dynamic states/choices, accessible forms/focus, responsive layout, escaping and clear errors.

## Acceptance cases

- C14-01: YAML loads eight initial states and nine edges with expected role/guard/effect metadata.
- C14-02: Happy path closes with five successful transition audit entries.
- C14-03: Rejection path includes reason/appeal instructions and eligible system closure.
- C14-04: Information loop resets assessment timer and clears stale completion before approval.
- C14-05: Illegal SUBMITTED-to-APPROVED edge reports source, target and available choices.
- C14-06: Unauthorized role fails at engine/application boundary without state/audit/outbox mutation.
- C14-07: Missing or invalid required documents fail with specific guard details.
- C14-08: Assessment cannot start without assigned assessor.
- C14-09: Incomplete report cannot approve/reject.
- C14-10: Amount equals limit passes; excess/negative/null/invalid currency fails appropriately.
- C14-11: Rejection and information request require nonblank reason/description.
- C14-12: Old information receipt fails; fresh server-stamped receipt permits return.
- C14-13: Payment initiation needs persisted request; closure needs confirmation/reference.
- C14-14: Appeal expiry boundary and member acknowledgement paths behave deterministically.
- C14-15: Three information requests succeed; fourth has exact escalation message; claims are independent.
- C14-16: Audit fields/order/claim scoping remain accurate and complete.
- C14-17: Runtime audit UPDATE/DELETE denied; owner trigger protects accidental mutation; no cascade.
- C14-18: Audit/outbox failure rolls back state, counter and payment request.
- C14-19: Rollback dispatches nothing; after-commit failure retains observable retry.
- C14-20: Concurrent same-version commands have one winner and no duplicate audit/payment.
- C14-21: Same actor/claim/key/payload replays result; different payload conflicts.
- C14-22: New state/edge works with configuration-only diff and dynamic interface options.
- C14-23: Duplicate/dangling/unknown guard/effect configuration fails startup clearly.
- C14-24: Terminal state has no outgoing choices.
- C14-25: HTTP401/403, ownership and system-role spoof protection.
- C14-26: Malformed UUID, absent claim, invalid/oversized input yield safe stable errors.
- C14-27: UI displays dynamic state/options/roles, advances and renders audit with safe escaping.
- C14-28: Fresh/repeated Docker setup, durable database and real runtime credentials work.
- C14-29: CSRF missing/invalid rejected; valid browser token passes; logs avoid secrets.

## Test execution and evidence

At least15 meaningful Java tests are required by the brief. Unit tests use JUnit5,
Mockito/AssertJ as appropriate. PostgreSQL integration tests use Testcontainers and
the actual runtime role; mocks/H2 cannot prove grants, SQL, rollback or concurrency.
Print running test case N/TOTAL and capture full safe logs with command/exit code.

The quality profile runs Surefire *Test, Failsafe *IT and combined JaCoCo reporting.
Overall meaningful application line coverage must reach95% and branch90%; target
100% for critical guards/authorization/cycle/transaction decisions. Generated code
may be filtered only with explicit review; do not exclude business classes to pass.
Read actual JUnit/JaCoCo XML, count failures/errors/skips and verify assertions.

```bash
mvn -B -Pquality clean verify
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker/compose.yml config --quiet
bash scripts/setup.sh
bash scripts/smoke.sh
bash scripts/run-scenarios.sh
```

Setup provisions only; tests are separate. Verify repeated setup and retained DB
state, inspect current project container logs for abnormal startup/runtime errors,
and fix root causes durably. Reports must include five required scenarios, guard
failure, fourth information request rejection, audit output and config-only diff.
Tie results to final source hashes. Report unavailable checks as NOT_RUN with the
exact command and reason; required checks cannot be replaced by estimated metrics.
Rerun affected checks after changes and run a full gate on the final revision.

# AI Challenge 14 — Claims Workflow Orchestrator

## Note

- You are expected to use AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) to complete this challenge.
- We evaluate your ability to decompose the problem, direct the AI tool effectively, and deliver a working solution.
- Please estimate and give us your timeline.
- If you have any issues, don't hesitate to contact us.

## Difficulty

Advanced · 5–8 hours

## Context

A claim moves through a defined lifecycle: Submitted → Documents Verified → Under Assessment → Approved/Rejected → Payment Initiated → Closed. Each transition has preconditions (must be true to proceed), triggers side effects (notifications, audit log entries), and may require specific roles to authorize. An incorrect transition — like approving a claim before documents are verified — can lead to fraud or compliance violations.

## Problem

Build a state machine-based workflow engine that orchestrates claim lifecycle transitions with preconditions, side effects, role-based authorization, and a complete audit trail.

## State Machine Definition

### States

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| SUBMITTED | Claim received, awaiting document verification |
| DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED | All required documents confirmed present and valid |
| UNDER_ASSESSMENT | Assessor is reviewing the claim |
| PENDING_INFO | Additional information requested from member |
| APPROVED | Claim approved for payment |
| REJECTED | Claim denied |
| PAYMENT_INITIATED | Payment processing started |
| CLOSED | Claim lifecycle complete |

### Transitions

| From | To | Preconditions | Side Effects | Authorized Roles |
|------|----|--------------|--------------|-----------------|
| SUBMITTED | DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED | All required documents present | Notify assessor team | document_clerk |
| DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED | UNDER_ASSESSMENT | Assessor assigned | Log assessment start time | team_lead |
| UNDER_ASSESSMENT | APPROVED | Assessment report complete, amount ≤ policy limit | Notify member, create payment request | assessor |
| UNDER_ASSESSMENT | REJECTED | Assessment report complete, rejection reason provided | Notify member with reason and appeal instructions | assessor |
| UNDER_ASSESSMENT | PENDING_INFO | Missing info description provided | Notify member with request details | assessor |
| PENDING_INFO | DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED | New documents/info received | Reset assessment timer | document_clerk |
| APPROVED | PAYMENT_INITIATED | Payment request created | Trigger payment system | finance |
| PAYMENT_INITIATED | CLOSED | Payment confirmed | Notify member with payment reference | finance |
| REJECTED | CLOSED | Appeal period expired OR member acknowledged | Archive claim | system |

## Requirements

### Core Engine
- State machine defined in configuration (JSON/YAML), not hardcoded in application logic
- Validate transitions: reject invalid transitions with a specific error explaining why
- Check preconditions before allowing a transition
- Execute side effects after a successful transition (mock implementations — log to console)
- Enforce role-based authorization — reject transitions from unauthorized roles

### Audit Trail
- Every transition logged with: timestamp, from_state, to_state, triggered_by (user ID + role), reason/notes
- Audit trail is immutable — entries cannot be modified or deleted
- Query audit trail by claim ID to see full history

### Cycle Detection
- The UNDER_ASSESSMENT → PENDING_INFO → DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED → UNDER_ASSESSMENT loop is allowed, but limit to 3 cycles maximum
- On the 4th attempt, reject the transition with "Maximum information requests exceeded — escalate to team lead"

### Test Scenarios

Implement and run 5 scenarios:

1. **Happy path**: SUBMITTED → DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED → UNDER_ASSESSMENT → APPROVED → PAYMENT_INITIATED → CLOSED
2. **Rejection path**: SUBMITTED → DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED → UNDER_ASSESSMENT → REJECTED → CLOSED
3. **Request more info loop**: SUBMITTED → DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED → UNDER_ASSESSMENT → PENDING_INFO → DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED → UNDER_ASSESSMENT → APPROVED → PAYMENT_INITIATED → CLOSED
4. **Invalid transition**: Attempt SUBMITTED → APPROVED (should fail with clear error)
5. **Unauthorized role**: Attempt a transition with the wrong role (should fail)

### Interface
- CLI or web UI to: view current state + valid transitions, advance a claim through states, view audit trail for a claim
- Show available transitions from current state (including which role is needed)

## Evaluation Criteria

- All 5 test scenarios produce correct results
- Invalid transitions are rejected with specific error messages (not generic "invalid transition")
- Preconditions are enforced (demonstrate with a case where precondition fails)
- Role authorization is enforced
- Audit trail is complete and accurate for all scenarios
- Cycle detection prevents infinite loops
- Adding a new state or transition requires only config changes (demonstrate with a diff)
- At least 15 tests covering valid transitions, invalid transitions, precondition failures, role authorization, and cycle detection

## Submission

- Push your project onto a GitHub repository
- Include the state machine config, test scenario results, and audit trail output

## Models

Select GPT6.1 SOL / Medium in the coordinator's actual Codex session. Every worker
and independent reviewer uses GPT6 Luna / Medium. Configuration samples are under
codex/config.toml and codex/agents/; merge them into a writable project .codex
configuration without replacing unrelated settings. The current protected .codex
has not been modified. The host collaboration tool can explicitly spawn Luna with
model=gpt-6-luna, reasoning_effort=medium and fork_turns=none.

Model names in prompts do not switch the running primary model. A host that cannot
provide the selected model must report the limitation rather than silently
substitute. Agents inherit host permissions. Official schema guidance:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents

## Reusable execution prompt

```text
Implement the requirement in rules/REQUIREMENT.md using AGENTS.md and rules/workflow/WORKFLOW.md.
Use SOL medium as coordinator and Luna medium for every worker/reviewer. Maintain
the to-do/dependency graph, freeze contracts, dispatch independent ready tasks,
keep one source writer and serial builds, get independent review, and accept only
actual passing checks on the reviewed source. Continue within the authorized scope.
Preserve my messages verbatim in the separate AI conversation log. Keep English
implementation, synchronized progress/history, current docs and honest NOT_RUN
results. Fix core causes and rerun affected tests.
```

## Workflow guard checks

Python3.11+ standard library only:

```bash
python3 scripts/workflow/verify_workflow.py
python3 scripts/workflow/verify_workflow.py --ready
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/workflow -p test_verify_workflow.py -v
```

Accepted evidence must cover each required command, matching source hash, real
report and independent reviewer. The validator cannot authenticate artifact/hash
provenance or the full status ledger. Coordinator verification remains required.
Java application results are separate from these Python workflow safeguard tests.

## Architecture, audit and capacity addendum

1. Add a runtime @Auditable(action, resource) method annotation and Spring aspect
   for selected claim writes. Persist supplementary system-operation records in a
   dedicated append-only PostgreSQL table. Keep claim_audit unchanged as the
   domain transition history. Include action/resource/resource ID, authenticated
   actor, correlation ID, outcome, safe error type and timestamp. Do not serialize
   method arguments by default; never record credentials, tokens, claim documents,
   or unrestricted fact payloads. Successful audit insertion participates in the
   same transaction as the write, so an unaudited successful write cannot commit.
   A rejected operation may receive a separately committed failure record without
   replacing the original business error.
2. Idempotency applies to every mutating claim operation (create, facts update,
   human transition and system transition). Keys are scoped by authenticated actor
   and operation/resource; a matching key and request fingerprint returns the
   original result without repeating domain or system audit rows. Reusing a key
   with a different request returns a stable conflict. Concurrent identical
   requests produce one durable mutation and one effective audit event. Preserve
   the existing transition replay behavior.
3. Keep this as one modular Java/PostgreSQL service. Do not add Kafka, RabbitMQ,
   gRPC, external RPC or another broker. The existing database outbox remains the
   local durable mechanism for mock Challenge 14 effects.
4. Create architecture and workflow diagrams as image files under
   docs/architecture/images/, with editable source beside each exported image.
   Diagrams must match the implemented system and include the audit/idempotency
   path, PostgreSQL transaction boundary, local outbox, and configured claim states.
5. Add a generic capacity profile for 100 and 500 concurrent HTTP clients. Include
   reproducible JMeter plans, the required Compose setup/smoke sequence, dataset
   preparation, duration/ramp/think-time settings, error/latency/throughput
   measurements, resource monitoring, and report locations. Provide a clearly
   labeled starting hardware profile for each target; it is a planning estimate,
   not a measured service guarantee.
6. Keep JaCoCo gates at least 95% line and 90% branch with no business-code
   exclusions. Add meaningful tests for new audit/idempotency paths and rerun the
   gates until the added code satisfies them. Run Compose smoke after setup and
   execute the 100/500-client JMeter profiles only on an explicitly prepared test
   environment. Record actual test, coverage, smoke and load results; label runs
   that cannot be performed NOT_RUN with the exact command and reason.
7. Update OpenAPI, architecture/security/testing/operations docs, history,
   changelogs, requirement and delivery manifest. Do not claim capacity, SLA or
   performance until the corresponding load plan has actually run.

def main() -> int:
    env_path = Path(os.environ.get("CLAIMS_ENV_FILE", ".env"))
    if not env_path.is_file():
        print("Missing .env; run bash scripts/setup.sh first.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    env = read_env(env_path)
    required = ("CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD", "CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD")
    if any(not env.get(name) or env[name].startswith("CHANGE_ME_") for name in required):
        print("Configured credentials are missing or still placeholders.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    port = env.get("SERVER_PORT", "8080")
    api = Api(os.environ.get("CLAIMS_API_BASE", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"), {
        "clerk": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "lead": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"],
        "assessor": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "finance": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"],
        "member-demo": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "system": env["CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD"],
    })
    total = 20
    case = 0
    run_tag = uuid.uuid4().hex

    def check(name: str, actual: int, expected: int) -> None:
        nonlocal case
        case += 1
        print(f"running test case {case}/{total}: {name}")
        if actual != expected:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: expected HTTP {expected}, received HTTP {actual}")

    try:
        status, _, _ = api.call(None, "GET", "/api/v1/claims?page=0&size=1")
        check("unauthenticated claims request is rejected", status, 401)

        status, csrf, _ = api.call("clerk", "GET", "/api/v1/session")
        check("authenticated session supplies CSRF token", status, 200)
        if not all(csrf.get(field) for field in ("csrfHeaderName", "csrfParameterName", "csrfToken")):
            raise RuntimeError("session did not return the expected CSRF contract")

        status, created, headers = api.call("member-demo", "POST", "/api/v1/claims", key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-create",
            csrf=csrf, body={"policyLimit": 500, "currency": "USD", "facts": {"requestedAmount": 125.50}})
        check("member creates claim", status, 201)
        claim_id = created["id"]
        if headers.get("Location", "").endswith(claim_id) is False:
            raise RuntimeError("create response Location does not identify the returned claim")

        status, replay, _ = api.call("member-demo", "POST", "/api/v1/claims", key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-create",
            csrf=csrf, body={"policyLimit": 500, "currency": "USD", "facts": {"requestedAmount": 125.50}})
        check("create idempotency replays the original claim", status, 201)
        if replay["id"] != claim_id:
            raise RuntimeError("idempotent create returned a different claim id")

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}")
        check("claim owner can read claim", status, 200)
        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/audit")
        check("claim owner can read audit", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-no-csrf", body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {}}})
        check("unsafe request without CSRF token is rejected", status, 403)

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-member-write-denied", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {"invoice": {"present": True}}}})
        check("member cannot edit submitted document roster", status, 403)

        status, _, _ = api.call("clerk", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-documents", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {"invoice": {"required": True, "present": True, "valid": True}}}})
        check("document clerk records complete document", status, 200)

        status, transitioned, _ = api.call("clerk", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-verify", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED", "expectedVersion": 1, "reason": "Documents verified", "facts": {}})
        check("document clerk verifies claim", status, 200)
        if transitioned["claim"]["version"] != 2:
            raise RuntimeError("document verification did not advance the claim version")

        status, _, _ = api.call("lead", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-assign", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 2, "facts": {"assessorId": "assessor"}})
        check("team lead assigns assessor", status, 200)

        status, started, _ = api.call("lead", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-start-assessment", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "UNDER_ASSESSMENT", "expectedVersion": 3, "reason": "Assigned", "facts": {}})
        check("team lead starts assessment", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("assessor", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-report", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 4, "facts": {"assessmentReport": {"complete": True}}})
        check("assigned assessor submits report", status, 200)

        status, approved, _ = api.call("assessor", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-approve", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "APPROVED", "expectedVersion": 5, "reason": "Covered", "facts": {}})
        check("assessor approves and persists payment request", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("finance", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-initiate-payment", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "PAYMENT_INITIATED", "expectedVersion": 6, "reason": "Dispatch", "facts": {}})
        check("finance dispatches payment via outbox", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("assessor", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/system-transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-forbidden-system", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "CLOSED", "expectedVersion": 7, "reason": "forbidden", "facts": {}})
        check("human identity cannot invoke system transition", status, 403)

        status, options, _ = api.call("finance", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions")
        check("finance can inspect transition options", status, 200)
        close_available = next((option.get("available", False) for option in options
                                if option.get("transitionId") == "close-paid-claim"), False)
        attempts = 0
        while not close_available and attempts < 30:
            time.sleep(1)
            status, options, _ = api.call("finance", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions")
            if status != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(f"payment confirmation poll returned HTTP {status}")
            close_available = next((option.get("available", False) for option in options
                                    if option.get("transitionId") == "close-paid-claim"), False)
            attempts += 1
        if not close_available:
            raise RuntimeError("payment outbox did not confirm within 30 seconds")
        status, closed, _ = api.call("finance", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-close-paid", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "CLOSED", "expectedVersion": 7, "reason": "Payment confirmed", "facts": {}})
        check("finance closes claim after outbox confirmation", status, 200)
        if closed["claim"]["state"] != "CLOSED":
            raise RuntimeError("claim did not reach CLOSED")

        status, claim_list, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", "/api/v1/claims?page=0&size=20")
        check("member list endpoint returns visible claims", status, 200)
        if not any(item["id"] == claim_id for item in claim_list["items"]):
            raise RuntimeError("created claim is absent from the member-visible list")

        status, audit, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/audit")
        check("complete lifecycle exposes claim transition audit", status, 200)
        if len(audit["items"]) < 5:
            raise RuntimeError("expected transition audit records were not persisted")
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as error:
        print(f"Scenario failure after {case}/{total} cases: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Completed {case}/{total} end-to-end API scenarios.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exercise the authenticated HTTP claim lifecycle without printing credentials or payloads."""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import http.cookiejar
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import uuid
from pathlib import Path


def read_env(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    values: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        values[key.strip()] = value.strip()
    return values


class Api:
    def __init__(self, base: str, passwords: dict[str, str]):
        self.base = base.rstrip("/")
        self.passwords = passwords
        self.cookies = http.cookiejar.CookieJar()
        self.opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(self.cookies))

    def call(self, username: str | None, method: str, path: str, *, body=None, key=None, csrf=None):
        headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
        if body is not None:
            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        if key:
            headers["Idempotency-Key"] = key
        if csrf:
            headers[csrf["csrfHeaderName"]] = csrf["csrfToken"]
        if username:
            auth = base64.b64encode(f"{username}:{self.passwords[username]}".encode()).decode()
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Basic {auth}"
        data = json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")).encode() if body is not None else None
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
        try:
            with self.opener.open(request, timeout=10) as response:
                content = response.read()
                return response.status, json.loads(content) if content else None, response.headers
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            content = error.read()
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(content) if content else None
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                parsed = None
            return error.code, parsed, error.headers


def main() -> int:
    env_path = Path(os.environ.get("CLAIMS_ENV_FILE", ".env"))
    if not env_path.is_file():
        print("Missing .env; run bash scripts/setup.sh first.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    env = read_env(env_path)
    required = ("CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD", "CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD")
    if any(not env.get(name) or env[name].startswith("CHANGE_ME_") for name in required):
        print("Configured credentials are missing or still placeholders.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    port = env.get("SERVER_PORT", "8080")
    api = Api(os.environ.get("CLAIMS_API_BASE", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"), {
        "clerk": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "lead": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"],
        "assessor": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "finance": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"],
        "member-demo": env["CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD"], "system": env["CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD"],
    })
    total = 20
    case = 0
    run_tag = uuid.uuid4().hex

    def check(name: str, actual: int, expected: int) -> None:
        nonlocal case
        case += 1
        print(f"running test case {case}/{total}: {name}")
        if actual != expected:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: expected HTTP {expected}, received HTTP {actual}")

    try:
        status, _, _ = api.call(None, "GET", "/api/v1/claims?page=0&size=1")
        check("unauthenticated claims request is rejected", status, 401)

        status, csrf, _ = api.call("clerk", "GET", "/api/v1/session")
        check("authenticated session supplies CSRF token", status, 200)
        if not all(csrf.get(field) for field in ("csrfHeaderName", "csrfParameterName", "csrfToken")):
            raise RuntimeError("session did not return the expected CSRF contract")

        status, created, headers = api.call("member-demo", "POST", "/api/v1/claims", key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-create",
            csrf=csrf, body={"policyLimit": 500, "currency": "USD", "facts": {"requestedAmount": 125.50}})
        check("member creates claim", status, 201)
        claim_id = created["id"]
        if headers.get("Location", "").endswith(claim_id) is False:
            raise RuntimeError("create response Location does not identify the returned claim")

        status, replay, _ = api.call("member-demo", "POST", "/api/v1/claims", key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-create",
            csrf=csrf, body={"policyLimit": 500, "currency": "USD", "facts": {"requestedAmount": 125.50}})
        check("create idempotency replays the original claim", status, 201)
        if replay["id"] != claim_id:
            raise RuntimeError("idempotent create returned a different claim id")

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}")
        check("claim owner can read claim", status, 200)
        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/audit")
        check("claim owner can read audit", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-no-csrf", body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {}}})
        check("unsafe request without CSRF token is rejected", status, 403)

        status, _, _ = api.call("member-demo", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-member-write-denied", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {"invoice": {"present": True}}}})
        check("member cannot edit submitted document roster", status, 403)

        status, _, _ = api.call("clerk", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-documents", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 0, "facts": {"documents": {"invoice": {"required": True, "present": True, "valid": True}}}})
        check("document clerk records complete document", status, 200)

        status, transitioned, _ = api.call("clerk", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-verify", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "DOCUMENTS_VERIFIED", "expectedVersion": 1, "reason": "Documents verified", "facts": {}})
        check("document clerk verifies claim", status, 200)
        if transitioned["claim"]["version"] != 2:
            raise RuntimeError("document verification did not advance the claim version")

        status, _, _ = api.call("lead", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-assign", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 2, "facts": {"assessorId": "assessor"}})
        check("team lead assigns assessor", status, 200)

        status, started, _ = api.call("lead", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-start-assessment", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "UNDER_ASSESSMENT", "expectedVersion": 3, "reason": "Assigned", "facts": {}})
        check("team lead starts assessment", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("assessor", "PUT", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/facts",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-report", csrf=csrf,
            body={"expectedVersion": 4, "facts": {"assessmentReport": {"complete": True}}})
        check("assigned assessor submits report", status, 200)

        status, approved, _ = api.call("assessor", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-approve", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "APPROVED", "expectedVersion": 5, "reason": "Covered", "facts": {}})
        check("assessor approves and persists payment request", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("finance", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-initiate-payment", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "PAYMENT_INITIATED", "expectedVersion": 6, "reason": "Dispatch", "facts": {}})
        check("finance dispatches payment via outbox", status, 200)

        status, _, _ = api.call("assessor", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/system-transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-forbidden-system", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "CLOSED", "expectedVersion": 7, "reason": "forbidden", "facts": {}})
        check("human identity cannot invoke system transition", status, 403)

        status, options, _ = api.call("finance", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions")
        check("finance can inspect transition options", status, 200)
        close_available = next((option.get("available", False) for option in options
                                if option.get("transitionId") == "close-paid-claim"), False)
        attempts = 0
        while not close_available and attempts < 30:
            time.sleep(1)
            status, options, _ = api.call("finance", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions")
            if status != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(f"payment confirmation poll returned HTTP {status}")
            close_available = next((option.get("available", False) for option in options
                                    if option.get("transitionId") == "close-paid-claim"), False)
            attempts += 1
        if not close_available:
            raise RuntimeError("payment outbox did not confirm within 30 seconds")
        status, closed, _ = api.call("finance", "POST", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/transitions",
            key=f"e2e-{run_tag}-close-paid", csrf=csrf,
            body={"targetState": "CLOSED", "expectedVersion": 7, "reason": "Payment confirmed", "facts": {}})
        check("finance closes claim after outbox confirmation", status, 200)
        if closed["claim"]["state"] != "CLOSED":
            raise RuntimeError("claim did not reach CLOSED")

        status, claim_list, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", "/api/v1/claims?page=0&size=20")
        check("member list endpoint returns visible claims", status, 200)
        if not any(item["id"] == claim_id for item in claim_list["items"]):
            raise RuntimeError("created claim is absent from the member-visible list")

        status, audit, _ = api.call("member-demo", "GET", f"/api/v1/claims/{claim_id}/audit")
        check("complete lifecycle exposes claim transition audit", status, 200)
        if len(audit["items"]) < 5:
            raise RuntimeError("expected transition audit records were not persisted")
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as error:
        print(f"Scenario failure after {case}/{total} cases: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Completed {case}/{total} end-to-end API scenarios.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

The database also enforces a unique receipt key, version checks, append-only audit triggers, and runtime-role column grants. A rejected operation may append a safe failure record through `REQUIRES_NEW` after its business transaction rolls back.

An approved claim writes a payment request in the mutation transaction. The configured payment trigger creates a local outbox row in that same transaction. A scheduled dispatcher leases due rows, invokes mock delivery after the original commit, confirms a payment reference, and records delivery or a retry time. No external broker is part of this design.

## API and observability

The API is rooted at `/api/v1`. Claim and audit collections use zero-based `page` (default 0), `size` (default 20, maximum 100), deterministic ordering, and typed count/page responses. Member ownership filtering remains in SQL. `X-Correlation-ID` accepts only bounded safe ASCII, otherwise receives a generated UUID; the same effective value is returned, logged, and passed to mutation audit. It is kept separate from Micrometer observation trace/span context. Actuator health is public with hidden details; other actuator routes, including Prometheus, require authentication.

## Diagrams and sources

- [Claims architecture diagram](images/claims-architecture.png) ([SVG](images/claims-architecture.svg), [editable Mermaid source](images/claims-architecture.mmd))

# Security design and verification

## Identity and authorization

The service uses HTTP Basic with server-side session-backed CSRF protection. The browser fetches a CSRF token before mutation. A domain `Actor` is derived only from the authenticated principal and authorities; request bodies cannot select roles or member identity. The `system` principal must have the protected system authority and is accepted only by the system-transition endpoint. Human mutation methods reject the system identity. Member-scoped claim reads and audit access apply ownership checks, and list/count SQL includes member scope. Runtime database credentials have narrower grants than the Liquibase schema owner.

The in-memory accounts (`clerk`, `lead`, `assessor`, `finance`, `member-demo`, `system`) are local Challenge 14 demonstration identities, not an enterprise identity provider. Human and system passwords come from separate environment variables. Startup fails for empty or `CHANGE_ME_` passwords. Compose binds the HTTP port to loopback by default. TLS termination, external identity, secret rotation, and production account provisioning are not included in this implementation.

## Request and data controls

- JSON parsing rejects unknown fields; JSON request bodies are capped at 65,536 bytes, including requests without a declared content length.
- `X-Correlation-ID` accepts only 1–128 safe ASCII characters. Invalid/missing values get a generated UUID. The exact effective value flows through response, logs, and mutation audit.
- Every mutating claim operation requires an idempotency key; actor, operation/resource scope, canonical fingerprint and response are persisted transactionally.
- Claim rows, immutable audit records, runtime grants and payment/outbox update columns are constrained in PostgreSQL. Domain audit and system-operation audit use append-only mutation triggers.
- Error responses use stable API codes and avoid returning internal SQL or exception details. Failure audit stores the error type, not request bodies, credentials, documents, or unrestricted facts.

## Security verification status

Actor identity derivation, correlation handling, request-size enforcement, and request/resource contract rules have unit coverage. Live API scenarios verified authentication failure, valid session CSRF bootstrap, rejection of missing CSRF, member restrictions, role-bound workflow operations, ownership reads, and audit visibility. PostgreSQL/Testcontainers verified runtime-role grants, append-only audit enforcement, idempotency receipt persistence/serialization, transactional rollback, and concurrent compare-and-set behavior. The independent integrated review found no remaining critical/high implementation issues. These checks are eviden…130 tokens truncated…wrapper bootstrap was not required for this run; a wrapper would still require Java and the Maven distribution/dependencies.

Create `.env` from `.env.example` and use `bash scripts/setup.sh` to generate bootstrap, migration and runtime database passwords before Compose starts. Set `CLAIMS_DEMO_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] and a separate `CLAIMS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD[REDACTED_SECRET] the application fails closed when either is blank or left at a `CHANGE_ME_` placeholder. Do not commit `.env`. Compose binds the service to loopback by default, runs PostgreSQL 16, grants Liquibase a schema-owner login, and gives the application a restricted runtime login. The bootstrap credential is reserved for first-time database initialization.

The intended sequence is:

```bash
bash scripts/setup.sh
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker/compose.yml up --build -d
bash scripts/smoke.sh
```

Docker daemon access is denied inside the default sandbox, so Docker commands were run only through approved escalated invocations; no socket permissions or daemon settings were changed. `bash scripts/setup.sh` succeeded three times, including the final image rebuild from normalized migration source against the existing volume. Both services reported healthy; existing claim rows were retained (four claims after the final unique scenario run). Liquibase ran five changesets on first startup and reported the database up to date on subsequent startup. The authenticated smoke check and 20-case API scenario run passed after final setup. Evidence is in `reports/verification/compose-repeat-setup.log`, `compose-final-setup.log`, `api-smoke-final.log`, and `e2e-scenarios-final.log`.

## Runtime behavior

Mutations write claim state, claim audit, system audit, idempotency receipt, and any payment/outbox evidence in a PostgreSQL transaction. The scheduled outbox dispatcher runs after commit, applies a configured lease and retry delay, and emits only mock Challenge 14 effects. Outbox delivered/failed counters and request observations are exposed through Micrometer; `/actuator/prometheus` remains authenticated. Public health output hides details.

Logs include method, path, status, duration, effective correlation ID, and trace/span IDs when provided by an observation tracing bridge. The application currently includes Micrometer observations and Prometheus metrics, but no tracing bridge dependency was resolved; observed `traceId` and `spanId` are null in unit output. Do not describe distributed tracing as verified.

## Verification limits

- The default sandbox blocks direct Docker socket and localhost access; approved escalated invocations work. No security controls were modified or bypassed.

Current app/database services are healthy. See the preserved container log evidence for exact chronology.

while True:
    stamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    stats=subprocess.run(['docker','stats','--no-stream','--format','{{json .}}'],capture_output=True,text=True)
    containers=[]

    query="SELECT json_build_object('active_connections',(SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname=current_database()),'transactions_committed',xact_commit,'transactions_rolled_back',xact_rollback,'outbox_pending',(SELECT count(*) FROM local_outbox WHERE delivered_at IS NULL),'outbox_failed',(SELECT count(*) FROM local_outbox WHERE delivered_at IS NULL AND attempts>1),'outbox_oldest_pending_seconds',(SELECT COALESCE(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM(clock_timestamp()-min(created_at))),0) FROM local_outbox WHERE delivered_at IS NULL)) FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname=current_database();"
    db=subprocess.run(['docker','compose','--env-file','.env','-f','docker/compose.yml','exec','-T','database','psql','-U','claims_bootstrap','-d','claims','-Atc',query],capture_output=True,text=True)

    except json.JSONDecodeError: db_data={'status':'PARSE_ERROR'}
    with open(out,'a') as f: f.write(json.dumps({'timestamp_utc':stamp,'containers':containers,'database':db_data})+'\n')

EOF
